companies.name: 011h
companies.one_liner: Snaps together homes for Europe's housing gap.
companies.solution: If homes can be built like well-planned kits, developers could know the cost, timeline and carbon footprint before breaking ground, rather than finding out as they go. That could help Europe build the affordable, lower-carbon homes it urgently needs, and build them faster than one-off projects allow. For the people waiting on a home, that is the difference between a project that takes years to start and one already underway.
companies.problem: Building apartments usually means a custom design every time, many separate contractors, and costs and timelines nobody can pin down until the work is done. 011h designs homes from a library of standard building parts, made in partner factories and assembled on site, with its own software planning the sequence. Because the same parts repeat from one project to the next, the cost and the carbon are known upfront rather than discovered along the way.

companies.name: 1KOMMA5
companies.one_liner: Makes powering up your house with solar actually accessible.
Turns carbon dioxide into stone.
companies.solution: If carbon can be turned into rock for good, storing it becomes a job that actually finishes rather than an obligation that outlasts the contract. That could make permanent carbon storage simpler, safer and easier to scale, especially in regions where the right rocks are plentiful. For the places sitting on those rocks, a quirk of local geology turns into steady work, and emitters gain somewhere to put their carbon.
companies.problem: Storing captured CO₂ usually means pumping it underground as a gas and watching the site for decades to make sure it stays put, with someone carrying the liability all that time. 44.01 mixes CO₂ with seawater and injects it into peridotite, a rock that reacts with it, turning the carbon into solid stone within months. Once the carbon has become mineral it is simply part of the rock, and the watching can stop.

companies.name: Absolute
companies.one_liner: AI using mother nature’s intelligence to grow fruits and veggies way faster.

companies.name: Aclarity
companies.one_liner: Removes "forever chemicals" from your water like they were never there.

companies.name: Ada Health
companies.one_liner: Saving patients years of life by shortening the time to diagnosis and treatment through AI.

companies.name: Aerleum
companies.one_liner: Turns toxic industrial emissions into building blocks for brand-new products.
companies.solution: Aerleum is a French climate tech startup specializing in converting atmospheric CO₂ into e-methanol using a proprietary single-reactor system.
companies.problem: Industries release massive amounts of harmful air pollutants like sulfur dioxide, which not only worsen climate change but also severely impact public health especially near industrial zones.
companies.description: Aerleum transforms toxic emissions into valuable materials using a circular process. By capturing pollutants such as sulfur dioxide, they upcycle what would be environmental waste into usable chemical feedstocks creating both a cleaner atmosphere and new economic opportunities.

companies.name: Aerones
companies.one_liner: Cleans and repairs massive wind turbines using giant robot drones.
companies.solution: Aerones develops robotic systems for the inspection, cleaning, and repair of wind turbines, enhancing maintenance efficiency and safety.
companies.problem: Wind energy is booming but maintaining the towering turbines is dangerous, slow, and costly. Many turbines run inefficiently or break down due to delays in maintenance, limiting clean energy output and driving up energy costs.
companies.description: Aerones replaces human climbers with robotic drones that clean, inspect, and repair wind turbines 3x faster and safer. By automating this process, they reduce turbine downtime, cut emissions, and boost clean energy performance scaling the future of renewables with sky-high precision.

companies.name: African Management Institute (AMI)
companies.one_liner: Empowers African businesses with hands-on learning tools that boost revenue and drive real growth.

companies.name: Again Bio
companies.one_liner: Turning pollution into products. Again turns waste into useful products, without breaking the bank or the planet.
companies.solution: Again is a Danish startup that converts industrial CO₂ emissions into valuable chemicals through a proprietary biomanufacturing process.
companies.problem: The chemical industry is one of the largest industrial carbon emitters globally. Traditional chemical manufacturing relies heavily on fossil fuels and conventional processes, contributing significantly to greenhouse gas emissions.
companies.description: Again offers a groundbreaking answer: a bio-fermentation platform that converts industrial CO₂ emissions into valuable, carbon-negative chemicals.

companies.name: AgriCarbon
companies.one_liner: Measures soil carbon at scale to unlock billions in climate finance.
companies.solution: Agricarbon is a UK-based company specializing in scalable, high-accuracy soil carbon measurement services to support carbon sequestration verification.
companies.problem: Soils are one of the largest carbon sinks on Earth, but we have no scalable, reliable way to measure how much carbon is actually being stored. Without this data, regenerative farmers can't get paid, and carbon markets lack trust and transparency.
companies.description: Agricarbon solves this with industrial-grade soil carbon measurement, using automated sampling and machine learning to deliver low-cost, high-accuracy carbon data at scale. This enables carbon credit systems to reward farmers for regenerating soil, unlocking a new economy for climate-positive agriculture.

companies.name: AgroLeague
companies.one_liner: What if, we connect small-scale farmers with agricultural experts over the internet?

companies.name: AI-BOB
companies.one_liner: Catches building errors before they're built
companies.solution: Catching mistakes on screen is far cheaper than fixing them on site. If checks like this become routine, buildings could be designed faster, approved more smoothly and built with less waste, time and cost. A rule missed at the drawing board costs an afternoon of redrawing, instead of a change order once the foundation has gone in, the site is full of people and the concrete has already been poured.
companies.problem: Sweden has replaced its detailed building code with rules based on performance, dropping the worked dimensions architects used to measure against, which leaves more room for interpretation and more room for mistakes. AI-BOB works inside architects' design software, checking a building design against the text of the regulations as it's drawn, flagging the clauses it fails and suggesting fixes. The drawing stays open the whole time.

companies.name: Air Protein
companies.one_liner: What If, We Use Carbon Captured From The Air To Create Food?

companies.name: AirForestry
companies.one_liner: Drones thin forests without damage
companies.solution: Drones could make gentle forest care possible in wet, steep and roadless areas that machines can't reach. Healthier forests, less soil damage and work that isn't held back by the weather: a lighter footprint for forestry. Stands skipped year after year because the ground would never carry a machine could come back into rotation, tended by something that lands nowhere and leaves no track behind it.
companies.problem: Thinning forests usually means driving harvesters and forwarders weighing tens of tonnes through them, which compacts soil, tears roots and leaves ruts that last for years, and can only be done in dry or frozen conditions. AirForestry uses electric drones that select a tree, grip the top, strip its branches, cut it near the base and lift the whole stem out to a roadside pile, without touching the forest floor. Onboard vision picks which trees to take.

companies.name: Airloom Energy
companies.one_liner: Harvests wind energy with tech that delivers turbine power at a fraction of the cost.

companies.name: Alcemy
companies.one_liner: Uses AI to make low-carbon cement as reliable as regular cement.
companies.solution: Software for cement and concrete producers that offers precise quality predictions for mixtures and their ingredients before shipping out products, enabling companies to counterbalance fluctuations in the limestone and the cement.
companies.problem: Cement is the second most consumed material on Earth, and a top contributor to global CO₂ emissions. Cutting its carbon footprint is critical, but making lower-carbon cement often compromises quality and consistency, deterring wide adoption in construction.
companies.description: Alcemy uses AI and real-time data to precisely control cement production so builders can use low-carbon blends with full confidence in strength and durability. Their tech transforms one of the world’s dirtiest industries into a climate solution, without sacrificing performance or safety.

companies.name: Alchemab Therapeutic
companies.one_liner: Designs antibodies that stop hard-to-treat diseases before you can say "hard-to-treat".

companies.name: Aleph Farms
companies.one_liner: Producing actual, real beef with no kills.

companies.name: Alight
companies.one_liner: What if, large corporations could go green and energy-independent by building their own solar parks?

companies.name: Allozymes
companies.one_liner: Creates custom enzymes that make manufacturing things cleaner and greener across all industries.

companies.name: Altruistiq
companies.one_liner: Leaving companies with no excuse to not lower their carbon footprint.

companies.name: Amatera
companies.one_liner: Coffee bred in years, not lifetimes.
companies.solution: As climate change reshapes where crops can grow, farmers need new varieties fast. Breeding in years rather than decades could help keep coffee, bananas and grapes thriving, and protect the livelihoods of the farmers who grow them. Crops that were never worth a breeding programme measured in lifetimes could become worth the effort, in exactly the places where growing conditions are shifting fastest.
companies.problem: Breeding a new coffee variety can take longer than a breeder's career, because each generation of plants has to grow and bear fruit before it can be judged, and the work sits mainly with public programmes on modest budgets. Amatera works with coffee, banana and grape at the single-cell stage, inducing variation and screening the resulting cell lines in the lab, then growing out only the most promising plants. The choosing happens before anything is planted.

companies.name: Amini
companies.one_liner: Maps climate and environmental data across Africa using AI to make informed environmental decisions.
companies.solution: Amini is a Kenyan climate-tech startup that leverages artificial intelligence to address Africa's environmental data scarcity
companies.problem: Africa faces immense climate, agricultural, and water challenges but lacks reliable environmental data to plan, adapt, and finance solutions. Without this information, businesses, governments, and farmers operate in the dark, widening the climate resilience gap.
companies.description: Amini uses AI and ground-level insights to deliver high-resolution, real-time environmental data across the African continent. Their platform unlocks better decisions for agriculture, carbon markets, and climate finance empowering an entire continent to leapfrog into a data-informed, climate-smart future.

companies.name: AMPD
companies.one_liner: Building mega-batteries that power entire buildings, 100% fossil-free.

companies.name: Ampd Energy
companies.one_liner: Powers cranes without the diesel.
companies.solution: If building sites can run on stored electricity, cities could become quieter and cleaner while they grow. Rules for low-emission construction would become practical to follow, and sites wouldn't have to wait for costly grid upgrades before ditching diesel. For the people living beside a build, the years it takes would sound different, the air on their street would be easier to breathe, and the quiet hours would stay quiet.
companies.problem: Construction sites usually run cranes and hoists on diesel generators sized for brief peaks, so they spend most of the day idling far below their rating, noisy and polluting, within earshot of everyone living nearby. Ampd Energy's sealed battery units replace those generators, charging from a small grid connection and delivering the bursts of power the machines need. There are no fuel deliveries to book and no refuelling to log.

companies.name: Ampersand
companies.one_liner: Doubles drivers' incomes with electric motorcycles while leapfrogging Africa into a zero-carbon future.

companies.name: Andes
companies.one_liner: What if, we create crops that clean the air as they grow?

companies.name: Anthro Energy
companies.one_liner: Makes batteries flexible, safe, and wearable just like the devices they power.
companies.solution: Anthro Energy develops advanced polymer electrolyte technology to create safer, flexible, and high-performance lithium-ion batteries​.
companies.problem: Traditional lithium-ion batteries are rigid, flammable, and fragile limiting innovation in wearables, flexible electronics, and next-gen devices. Their bulky form factor and safety risks pose major barriers to progress.
companies.description: Anthro Energy has developed a new class of flexible, solid-state batteries that bend, twist, and stretch without breaking or catching fire. Their chemistry breakthrough enables safer, more adaptable power sources for everything from medical wearables to foldable devices unlocking a new era in electronics.

companies.name: Antora Energy
companies.one_liner: Storing and distributing renewable energy through blocks of glowing carbon.

companies.name: Apollo Agriculture
companies.one_liner: Helping small farmers in Africa grow their harvest and revenue with financing, insurance, and training.

companies.name: Arbonics
companies.one_liner: Helps landowners turn forests into carbon income without guesswork.
companies.solution: Landowners across Europe hold a powerful climate asset forests. But due to complex carbon standards, technical barriers, and opaque marketplaces, most can’t access the booming carbon credit economy. That’s a huge missed opportunity for both climate and rural income.
companies.problem: Arbonics offers a full-stack platform that uses ecological data, satellite imagery, and machine learning to help landowners measure, verify, and monetize their carbon storage. With tools that are radically simpler and more transparent, they turn forests into income engines while scaling nature-based carbon removal.
companies.description: Arbonics provides landowners and credit buyers with a verified, databacked way of collaborating at scale to remove carbon and protect biodiversity through forestry solutions.

companies.name: Arborea
companies.one_liner: What if, we could slow down climate change by growing edible superfoods?

companies.name: ARC Ride
companies.one_liner: Trades petrol fumes for a charged battery
companies.solution: With enough swap stations, going electric becomes as easy as filling up with petrol, and cheaper. That could put more money in riders' pockets, cut fuel costs and clean up city air across Africa, where millions earn their living on two wheels. Every move in the pump price comes straight out of a rider's daily takings today, and stations sitting close enough together take that worry off the road for good.
companies.problem: For motorbike taxi riders in Kenya, electric bikes are hard to afford because the battery is so expensive, and nobody can lose hours to charging in the middle of a working day. ARC Ride builds electric motorbikes and three-wheelers in Nairobi and runs a network where riders swap a flat battery for a charged one in minutes, paying per swap. The battery stops being something a rider has to buy before they can start work.

companies.name: Arcadia
companies.one_liner: Connects people who cannot afford solar with access to clean energy sources.

companies.name: ArkeaBio
companies.one_liner: A vaccine for the climate, given to cows.
companies.solution: A simple injection, given during routine vet visits, could reach cattle anywhere, including the grazing herds that no current solution touches. That could make cutting methane from livestock possible worldwide, not just on indoor farms. Veterinary channels already reach almost every country, including the ones where herds are still growing, so a cow out on grass would get the same care as one kept inside.
companies.problem: Cows release large amounts of methane, a powerful greenhouse gas, produced by microbes in their stomachs. Current solutions are feed additives that need to be mixed into every meal, which doesn't work for grazing cattle. ArkeaBio is developing a vaccine that trains the cow's immune system to reduce those methane-producing microbes, with the antibodies carried into the stomach in the saliva a cow already makes in great volume.

companies.name: Arnergy
companies.one_liner: Delivers solar power to businesses in Nigeria where the grid fails daily.
companies.solution: Replacing fossil fuel generators with modularized solar +lithium ion storage systems in emerging markets
companies.problem: Millions of businesses across Nigeria and sub-Saharan Africa suffer from unreliable electricity, leading to massive productivity losses, dependence on polluting diesel generators, and limited growth opportunities.
companies.description: Arnergy provides solar energy systems with smart batteries, designed specifically for the African energy reality. Their decentralized solar solutions empower SMEs, clinics, and schools with affordable, consistent, clean power replacing diesel and catalyzing economic growth from the ground up.

companies.name: Arpeggio Bio
companies.one_liner: Leveraging AI to find a cure for cancer.

companies.name: Arsenale Bioyards
companies.one_liner:
Arsenale’s proprietary end-to-end platform makes biomanufacturing via precision fermentation economically viable 
at industrial scale for the very first time.
companies.solution: Arsenale Bioyards is an Italian biotech startup developing a full-stack biomanufacturing platform that integrates AI, precision fermentation, and modular infrastructure to scale sustainable alternatives to petrochemicals and animal-derived products
companies.problem: Biomanufacturing especially precision fermentation holds the promise of replacing petrochemical and animal-derived products with cleaner alternatives. Yet, it’s held back by immense hurdles: high costs, slow or unpredictable scaling, and fragmented systems that fail to bridge lab innovation with industrial reality.
companies.description: Arsenale Bioyards builds a neo-industrial, fully integrated biomanufacturing platform that harnesses hardware, data, and AI from the lab straight through to industrial production.

companies.name: Asilimia
companies.one_liner: What if, we build a cutting-edge digital finance platform for small-time businesses in Africa?

companies.name: Asimov
companies.one_liner: Turning genetic engineering into a precise science, making DNA design as easy as software coding.

companies.name: AssetCool
companies.one_liner: Sunscreen for the power grid.
companies.solution: Building new power lines takes years. Upgrading existing ones in place could free up capacity quickly, letting more clean energy onto the grid now, using the towers and wires we already have. No new right of way, no land to negotiate and no circuit switched out while crews string wire: capacity added a line at a time, on the grid that already runs past everybody's window and into the places waiting to connect.
companies.problem: Power lines can only carry so much electricity before they heat up and sag toward the ground, which limits how much new wind and solar power can connect. AssetCool sends a robot along live power lines to coat them with a surface that reflects sunlight and releases heat, so the lines stay cooler and carry more power. Raising that ceiling has usually meant stringing new wire along the same towers, priced by the mile and planned over years.

companies.name: Astranis
companies.one_liner: Satellites to connect billions of people without access to internet.

companies.name: Ataraxis
companies.one_liner: Transforming Cancer Care with AI Precision Medicine.
companies.solution: Ataraxis AI, a spin-off from NYU, creates AI-powered diagnostic tools that combine different types of patient data to improve cancer diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment decisions.
companies.problem: Traditional cancer diagnostics, particularly molecular genomic tests, come with significant limitations: they often require consuming precious tissue, take too long, are expensive, and offer only limited accuracy or scope.
companies.description: Ataraxis AI is building the future of precision oncology with AI-native, multi-modal diagnostic tools that deliver faster, smarter, and more personalized insights.

companies.name: Ataraxis AI
companies.one_liner: Reads a biopsy to predict who needs chemo.
companies.solution: If a slide a hospital already has can produce this kind of risk estimate within days, more patients could get personalised treatment decisions sooner, including those with cancer types current tests don't cover. Some could be spared chemotherapy that was never going to help them. For someone waiting after a biopsy, the answer would come back in the days after diagnosis rather than the weeks of waiting the old route takes.
companies.problem: Deciding whether a breast cancer patient needs chemotherapy often means sending tissue to a specialist lab and waiting around two weeks, and the test doesn't cover every type of breast cancer. Ataraxis AI uses AI to read the biopsy slide a hospital already has and estimate how likely the cancer is to return. It reads the shape of the tumour alongside basic clinical details, so patients whose cancer sits outside today's test are no longer treated on group averages.

companies.name: Augmenta
companies.one_liner: Using AI to automatically design sustainable houses in just a few hours.

companies.name: Auron Therapeutics
companies.one_liner: Flipping cancer treatment by turning malignant cells back to normal.

companies.name: Autochek
companies.one_liner: Making electric car ownership in Africa as simple and affordable as a few clicks.

companies.name: Avelios
companies.one_liner: Brings hospital software into the 21st century creating sustainable AI driven healthcare.
companies.solution: Avelios Medical is a German healthtech startup offering a modular, AI-integrated hospital information system to modernize healthcare IT infrastructure
companies.problem: Hospitals rely on outdated, fragmented software systems that slow down care, waste resources, and generate mountains of emissions through inefficient processes and hardware-heavy infrastructure especially in high-volume, high-stress environments like surgical clinics.
companies.description: Avelios builds modular, cloud-native hospital software that streamlines patient care while drastically cutting energy use and IT overhead. By digitizing clinical workflows and integrating sustainability into the operating system of care, Avelios turns hospitals into smart, climate-resilient health systems.

companies.name: Avelios Medical
companies.one_liner: Updates hospital software so care keeps running.
companies.solution: When patient records are clear and consistent from the start, the same information can support billing, safety checks and medical research without a separate project to clean it up first. Hospitals could learn faster from their own data, helping doctors make better decisions for patients. For anyone being treated, that means the care they get is shaped by what the hospital has already learned from everyone who came before them.
companies.problem: Many hospitals in German-speaking countries have to replace their core software in the coming years, usually in one risky switchover prepared for well over a year, with every ward moving at once. Avelios offers a modern hospital system that can be introduced step by step, and records information in a structured way that different tools can understand. Ward rounds, medication, theatre lists and billing are all written down in shared clinical terms as the work happens.

companies.name: Axle Energy
companies.one_liner: Home devices, standing in for gas plants.
companies.solution: Millions of homes already hold a huge amount of flexible energy in their garages and utility rooms, needing no new site, no permit and no construction. If it can be put to work, the grid could rely less on fossil fuel plants for peak demand, and families could earn money for helping keep the lights on. The car charging overnight and the heating that pauses for an hour become a quiet contribution from an ordinary street.
companies.problem: When electricity demand peaks, gas plants are paid to fire up, while electric cars, home batteries and heat pumps sit idle, shut out of markets built for power stations. Axle Energy gives the companies that make and supply these devices one connection into electricity markets, so they can shift their energy use when it helps the grid, and households get paid for it. One connection registers a device, works out what it can shift, offers that to the market and sends the money back to the household.

companies.name: Axmed
companies.one_liner: Makes sure life-saving medicine gets to people who need it, no matter where they live.

companies.name: Azimov
companies.one_liner: Turning genetic engineering into a precise science, making DNA design as easy as software coding.

companies.name: Back Market
companies.one_liner: What if, we could make second hand gadgets the first hand choice?

companies.name: Bamboo
companies.one_liner: Bringing Wall Street to the African continent, one trade at a time.

companies.name: BanQu
companies.one_liner: What if, we use a blockchain to protect the world's poorest from fraud?

companies.name: Bees & Bears
companies.one_liner: Puts solar within reach of any household
companies.solution: When financing is as easy as signing the quote, far more families can make the switch to clean energy at home, deciding during the visit rather than months later. That could speed up the spread of solar and heat pumps well beyond households with savings to spare. It would show up in ordinary streets, on the roofs and in the cellars of families who had always assumed this was something other people could afford.
companies.problem: Many households want solar panels or a heat pump but can't pay the full cost upfront, and applying for a loan separately takes time while the quote goes stale and the project drifts. Bees & Bears lets installers offer financing on the spot during the sales visit, with a partner bank handling the credit. The installer builds the instalment plan in the same tool that produces the quote, and the bank pays the work out in stages as the job progresses.

companies.name: Beyond Aero
companies.one_liner: Making hydrogen-powered jets that travels five times farther than battery planes.

companies.name: BeZero Carbon
companies.one_liner: A credit ratings agency for carbon credits, to prevent climate fraud.

companies.name: Big Health
companies.one_liner: What if, we use digital therapeutics to treat insomnia and anxiety?

companies.name: Biobot Analytics
companies.one_liner: Turning wastewater into a frontline defense against COVID-19, RSV, and more, protecting communities with recycled water.

companies.name: Biofourmis
companies.one_liner: What if, we could predict and prevent serious medical problems with the help of data science and wearables?

companies.name: Biographica
companies.one_liner: Gives crop breeding a search engine.
companies.solution: If breeders can find the right genes faster, they can improve more traits in more crops, including the minor crops and vegetables grown by smaller farmers that rarely get attention today. That could mean hardier harvests as the climate changes. For a family farming a few acres in a drying season, it is the difference between a crop that copes with the weather it now gets and one bred for somewhere else.
companies.problem: Finding the genes behind useful crop traits, like drought tolerance, is slow: each candidate gene can take a full growing season to test, and most turn out to be dead ends. Biographica uses AI to predict which genes matter most, then tests the shortlist in real plants and learns from the results. The models read protein structures, regulatory DNA, gene networks and published research, and every field result sharpens the next prediction.

companies.name: Bionaut Labs
companies.one_liner: Sending tiny robots into your body to deliver medicine.

companies.name: Biorce
companies.one_liner: Gives drug trials an AI layer so treatments reach patients sooner.
companies.solution: Better-designed trials mean new treatments reach patients sooner, because a flawed assumption surfaces in review rather than in a clinic full of enrolled patients. It could also make studies for rare diseases and small patient groups more feasible, the ones that never begin because recruiting them looks impossible, giving more people a chance at new therapies. For a family living with a condition almost nobody studies, that is a trial worth starting at all.
companies.problem: Clinical trials are often designed on past experience, and flaws only show up once patients are enrolled, leading to costly changes, fresh ethics review and months of delay. Biorce uses AI trained on past trials to test a study's design before it starts, spotting problems with eligibility, timelines and recruitment early. It also points to the clinics that have found this kind of patient before, so the plan meets the people it was written for.
companies.description: Enter Biorce, a Barcelona-based healthtech startup founded in 2024 by [name] and [name].  Their mission? To transform clinical trial design with AI.

companies.name: BIORESTORE
companies.one_liner: What if, we make people buy less clothes by creating better detergent?

companies.name: BIOSORRA
companies.one_liner: Bakes nutshell waste into carbon-rich soil.
companies.solution: Very little carbon removal happens in Africa today, where a single corporate purchase can count among the largest deals on the continent. If this approach spreads to nut, coffee, cocoa and sugar processors across the tropics, farm waste could become a source of healthier soil, local jobs and trusted carbon removal, paid for by the buyers rather than the farmers. The crops the world already buys would leave behind better ground and steadier harvests for the people who grow them.
companies.problem: In Kenya, nutshells and husks from crop processing are often burned or dumped at the mill gate, releasing their carbon within hours, while nearby farmers struggle with worn-out soil. BIOSORRA heats that waste in a unit it built itself, turning it into biochar: a charcoal-like material that improves soil and locks carbon away for the long term. The residue and the tired fields sit a few kilometres apart, and this is what joins them.

companies.name: BlocPower
companies.one_liner: What if, we could make every apartment block run on solar energy?

companies.name: Bloom Biorenewables
companies.one_liner: What if, we could use plants instead of petroleum to make the stuff we need?

companies.name: Bluu Seafood
companies.one_liner: Actual real seafood without killing any fish.

companies.name: Bluum Bio
companies.one_liner: Boosting nature’s cleanup crew with biotech that cleans soil, air, and water faster than a jet sweep.

companies.name: Blykalla
companies.one_liner: Nuclear power, built on an assembly line.
companies.solution: If reactors can be made in series and delivered where they're needed, clean, reliable power could sit right next to the steel mills, ports and data centres that depend on it. Nuclear energy could become something businesses order and receive, not decades-long national projects carried by a whole country's balance sheet. For the towns built around those works, it would mean the furnaces and the jobs stay, and the smoke above them does not.
companies.problem: Industries and data centres need clean power around the clock, but today's nuclear plants are huge, one-off projects that take many years to build. Blykalla is developing small nuclear reactors cooled by molten lead, using a special steel it developed to withstand the coolant, designed to be built in factories. A steel mill wanting round-the-clock carbon-free power has no supplier at its own size, so it waits in a grid queue or burns gas.

companies.name: Boston Metal
companies.one_liner: Making metal sustainable by decarbonising the steel industry.

companies.name: bound4blue
companies.one_liner: Wind power for the ships that move the world.
companies.solution: The ships sailing today will be around for decades, and they will keep burning oil unless something changes on the vessels that exist now. If modern sails can be fitted during routine maintenance, existing fleets could cut fuel use and emissions right away, bringing wind power back to the ocean in a new form, fitted in a drydock slot a ship was booked into anyway. The trade that carries almost everything we own would move again partly on weather.
companies.problem: Cargo ships run almost entirely on fossil fuel, and cleaner fuels are still scarce and expensive, with most of them needing a new hull to burn. bound4blue fits ships with tall, rigid sails that use a fan to hold the airflow, so they generate strong pushing power from the wind and adjust themselves without the crew. Every sail keeps working at angles where a soft sail would stall, taking a share off the fuel bill of a ship already at sea.

companies.name: Brighte
companies.one_liner: Makes it possible for anyone to afford a transition to solar.

companies.name: Brimstone
companies.one_liner: What If, We Build Houses That Clean The Air?

companies.name: Brineworks
companies.one_liner: Ultra low-cost Direct Air Capture company.
companies.solution: Brineworks is a Dutch climate-tech startup focused on developing a highly efficient, patent-pending saltwater electrolyzer. This technology enables the low-cost extraction of carbon dioxide (CO₂) and hydrogen (H₂) directly from the atmosphere, providing essential feedstocks for the production of e-fuels.
companies.problem: Traditional Direct Air Capture of CO₂ is prohibitively expensive estimated at $230–$630 per metric ton. These methods are often energy-intensive, require costly materials, and lack scalability or flexibility for remote or renewable-powered operation.
companies.description: Brineworks uses a Direct Air Capture solution that can operate anywhere and reach ultra-low costs around the world, with a clear path to <$100/ton-CO₂ due to a breakthrough electrolyzer technology.

companies.name: BURN
companies.one_liner: What if, we could save lives by making cheap and energy-efficient cookstoves available at scale?

companies.name: C The Signs
companies.one_liner: What if, we use big data to find cancer early?

companies.name: C16 Biosciences
companies.one_liner: Brewing the future of fats, leaving palm oil in the past.

companies.name: Candidly
companies.one_liner: Helping people not get completely screwed over by their student loans.

companies.name: CanopyLAB
companies.one_liner: What if, we create a social network dedicated to learning?

companies.name: Caption Health
companies.one_liner: Marrying AI and ultrasound for ultra-early disease detection.

companies.name: Captura
companies.one_liner: Using renewable energy to extract carbon from oceans.

companies.name: CarbonRe
companies.one_liner: Uses AI to slash industrial CO₂ emissions without rebuilding factories.
companies.solution: Uses AI-driven solutions to help industries like cement, steel, and energy reduce carbon emissions and improve efficiency
companies.problem: Heavy industries like cement and steel are responsible for over 20% of global emissions. But modernizing or replacing these massive facilities is expensive, slow, and disruptive leaving many companies stuck with dirty processes.
companies.description: CarbonRe’s AI platform integrates into existing industrial systems and optimizes them in real-time dramatically reducing energy use and carbon emissions specially in the cement industry . It’s like giving factories a climate-smart brain, cutting costs and emissions without expensive infrastructure upgrades.

companies.name: CareAcademy
companies.one_liner: Elevating healthcare by cultivating highly skilled caregivers through a digital training platform.

companies.name: Ceezer
companies.one_liner: Turning carbon credits into a clear, data-driven path to net-zero.

companies.name: Cellino
companies.one_liner: Making groundbreaking cell therapy to cure some of the toughest diseases - not just for the super-rich.

companies.name: Cemvision
companies.one_liner: Cement, baked without cooking the planet
companies.solution: Cement is everywhere, so cleaner cement could make a real dent in global emissions without bolting new equipment onto the kilns we already have. Turning industrial waste into a building material also means fewer quarries opened and fewer heaps left beside the mills, laying the foundations for a cleaner construction industry. The homes, bridges and schools still to be built would cost the air a good deal less.
companies.problem: Making cement releases about seven per cent of the world's carbon dioxide, mostly from heating limestone and from the fuel burned to drive that reaction. Cemvision makes cement from steel industry slag and other industrial by-products instead, using an electric kiln and avoiding most of the emissions that limestone gives off. Much of that waste gave up its carbon in an earlier furnace, so the reaction simply never happens again.

companies.name: Cerebral
companies.one_liner: What if, we could treat depression, anxiety and insomnia with a smartphone app?

companies.name: CH4 Global
companies.one_liner: Reducing emissions by making cows burp and fart less.

companies.name: Charm Industrial
companies.one_liner: Buries carbon back where the oil came from.
companies.solution: If this can be done wherever forests are thinned and crops are harvested, waste that currently goes up in smoke could become permanent carbon removal, while helping fund the forest care that protects communities from wildfires. For the crews who do that thinning, and for the towns downhill from them, a pile of brush stops being a chore to burn and becomes part of what pays for the work of keeping the woods around them safe.
companies.problem: When forests are thinned to reduce wildfire risk, the leftover branches are usually burned in open piles, and crop leftovers are left to rot, releasing their carbon either way. Charm turns this plant waste into a carbon-rich liquid and pumps it deep underground into regulated wells, where it stays for good. The waste is heated without oxygen until it breaks down, and once the liquid is in the well it sinks and hardens, putting the carbon back below the ground it came from.
companies.description: Charm Industrial converts crop residues into a stable, carbon-rich bio-oil and injects it deep underground, where it can stay for thousands of years. It’s fast, scalable, and measurable transforming waste into one of the world’s most effective carbon removal methods.

companies.name: Chinova Bioworks
companies.one_liner: Natural protection that keeps your food fresh, without the synthetic stuff.

companies.name: Clarity AI
companies.one_liner: AI-driven insights to make sustainability your default setting in investing, shopping, and beyond.

companies.name: CLER
companies.one_liner: Spins pollutants out of the air, no filters needed
companies.solution: Air cleaning without filters to replace means lower energy use, less waste and fewer maintenance visits. Kitchens and factories could keep their air clean all the time, improving working conditions and reducing fire risk. Extraction could run at full strength through the whole year instead of fading between service calls, which for the cooks on the line and the crews on the floor means cleaner air to breathe for a whole shift.
companies.problem: Commercial kitchens and industrial buildings use filters to catch grease and dust, but filters clog quickly, use more energy as they fill and need frequent replacing. CLER spins the air so fast that grease and particles separate out and drain away, with no filters needed. With nothing loading up, the fans move the same air on the same power, and the panels that used to be swapped out and sent to landfill are gone from the job altogether.

companies.name: Clexbio
companies.one_liner: Growing lab-made tissues that could treat diseases once thought impossible to cure.

companies.name: Climate X
companies.one_liner: Forecasts how climate change will impact businesses by advanced analytics allowing informed decisions and better solutions.
companies.solution: Climate X is a purpose-driven data company delivering location-specific risk ratings and loss estimates on physical assets for extreme weather events linked to climate change.
companies.problem: As climate risks escalate floods, heatwaves, wildfires governments and businesses urgently need to understand how these threats affect physical assets. Yet traditional climate models are too slow, coarse, or inaccessible for real-world decisions.
companies.description: Climate X delivers hyper-local, asset-level climate risk projections up to 2100. Their platform combines data science, climate modeling, and geospatial AI to predict how specific locations will fare under different climate scenarios empowering financial institutions, cities, and developers to protect and future-proof what matters most.

companies.name: ClimateView
companies.one_liner: Creating blueprints for cities to become their most sustainable self.

companies.name: Climeworks
companies.one_liner: Factories for sucking CO2 from the air 24/7.

companies.name: Clippership
companies.one_liner: Revolutionizes sea freight with zero-emission, wind-powered container ships.
companies.solution: Clippership is a U.S.-based startup developing autonomous, wind-powered cargo vessels to revolutionize sustainable maritime freight.
companies.problem: Global shipping accounts for nearly 3% of CO₂ emissions more than all of aviation. Despite growing demand for greener logistics, the industry remains dependent on heavy fuel oil and diesel engines, with few scalable alternatives.
companies.description: Clippership designs zero-emission container vessels powered by advanced wind propulsion and battery-electric systems. By reimagining maritime freight for the renewable era, they’re not just decarbonizing cargo they’re setting sail for a fossil-free shipping future.

companies.name: Commons
companies.one_liner: Helping you track, reduce and offset your own carbon footprint.

companies.name: Commonwealth Fusion Systems
companies.one_liner: Removing the need for fossil fuels by creating abundant and clean fusion technology.

companies.name: Constellr
companies.one_liner: Preventing wildfires with the help of satellites.

companies.name: Convoy
companies.one_liner: What if, we ensure freight trucks never travel with any empty space?

companies.name: Cradle
companies.one_liner: Speeds protein design for medicine and cleaner materials
companies.solution: If AI-guided design becomes routine, small teams could create enzymes and antibodies that once needed huge industrial labs, and could chase several properties at once rather than one at a time. That opens the door to new treatments, and to making everyday materials with biology instead of oil. For the rest of us it shows up quietly, in medicines that arrive sooner and in ordinary things grown rather than drilled for.
companies.problem: Designing better proteins, for medicines or greener materials, is slow: scientists make random changes and test the results, often for years. Cradle's AI suggests promising protein designs, learns from each round of lab results, and helps teams get to a better protein in far fewer steps. A team names the properties it wants, the model proposes variants, a batch is made and measured at the bench, and those measurements feed straight into the next round.
companies.description: Cradle Bio uses generative AI to help scientists design and validate new proteins in a fraction of the time. By simulating evolution and optimizing for function, stability, and sustainability, Cradle accelerates biomanufacturing breakthroughs from low-carbon materials to next-gen therapeutics.

companies.name: Credrails
companies.one_liner: Fuels Africa’s digital revolution, giving businesses the financial data they need to grow faster and smarter.

companies.name: Curacel
companies.one_liner: Making vital insurances available to everyone in Africa.

companies.name: Cure51
companies.one_liner: Studies people who beat cancer then turns their biology into cures.
companies.solution: the first worldwide database of Cancer survivors to leverage their exceptional biological features and find new drugs.
companies.problem: Despite decades of research, cancer remains one of the leading causes of death worldwide. While vast resources go into studying cancer cells, we know shockingly little about the biology of those who survive the disease against the odds.
companies.description: Cure51 flips the script by building the world’s first global biobank of “exceptional responders”, cancer patients who survive long beyond expectations. By decoding their biology, they’re unlocking new cancer therapies and giving science a radically hopeful new source of insight: human resilience.

companies.name: CuspAI
companies.one_liner: Designs next-gen materials with AI to solve climate at the atomic level.
companies.solution: search engine for materials that can help advance environmental sustainability, by enabling users to input the properties they want a material to have, and then generate the chemical composition needed to achieve it
companies.problem: Humanity needs entirely new materials to solve climate challenges like capturing carbon, storing energy, or replacing polluting chemicals. But discovering and testing these materials through lab experiments is slow, costly, and full of dead ends.
companies.description: CuspAI is building a generative AI platform that designs breakthrough materials on demand. Trained on physics, chemistry, and real-world data, their models can simulate and optimize new substances, radically accelerating the race to climate-saving innovation.

companies.name: Cylib
companies.one_liner: Recycles EV batteries with nearly zero waste and total resource recovery.
companies.solution: End-2-End Battery Recycling
companies.problem: Electric vehicle batteries are essential for decarbonization but when they reach end-of-life, they create a new environmental problem. Existing recycling methods are inefficient, energy-intensive, and often leave valuable materials lost or contaminated.
companies.description: Cylib has developed a water-based, energy-efficient recycling process that recovers all critical raw materials like lithium, cobalt, and graphite from EV batteries. Their closed-loop system makes battery production more sustainable and less dependent on mining, setting a new gold standard for circular mobility.

companies.name: D.light
companies.one_liner: What if, we build cheap and simple solar systems to make anyone, anywhere energy independent?

companies.name: Dandelion Energy
companies.one_liner: Making households less dependent on oil and natural gas through geothermal energy.

companies.name: Decade
companies.one_liner: Making the clean energy shift make business sense.
companies.solution: Providing comprehensive electrification solutions for logistics companies aiming to transition their fleets to electric vehicles (EVs) by offering end-to-end services, including infrastructure design, financing, installation, and operations, to facilitate a seamless and cost-effective shift to electric transportation
companies.problem: Electrifying logistics fleets is crucial for reducing transportation emissions but it’s notoriously complex and expensive. Logistics providers face fragmented systems involving grid access, charging hardware, renewable energy integration, and management software all of which create cost, reliability, and execution hurdles.
companies.description: Decade Energy is a Paris-based innovator transforming this challenge into opportunity through holistic, turnkey electrification solutions for depot operators and transport companies.

companies.name: Decade Energy
companies.one_liner: Wires up the grid electric trucks need
companies.solution: If charging infrastructure becomes a service, logistics companies can electrify their fleets as fast as they can buy trucks, rather than waiting on a connection date nobody in the business controls. That could speed up the shift to cleaner freight across Europe, cutting emissions and noise on the roads. For anyone living along a freight route, that arrives as quieter mornings and cleaner air at the roadside.
companies.problem: Electric trucks are ready, but the depots they charge at often aren't. Grid connections can take years and the engineering is complex. Decade Energy builds and runs the full charging setup, including grid connection, batteries, solar and chargers, and depots pay a monthly fee rather than buying the equipment. It keeps ownership and operates the site, so the queue, the engineering and the upkeep sit with people who do this every day.

companies.name: Deep Genomics, INC.
companies.one_liner: AI making tailored drugs that your body won't reject.

companies.name: Deepcell
companies.one_liner: Blending AI, microfluidics, and optics to revolutionize how we see and understand cell science.

companies.name: Deepull
companies.one_liner: Deepull identifies sepsis pathogens directly from blood in just one hour.
companies.solution: Deepull’s UllCORE system offers a fully automated, culture‑free molecular test that extracts microbial DNA from ~8 mL of whole blood, delivering identification of ~95% of sepsis pathogens plus resistance genes in ~1 hour, outperforming blood cultures and enabling timely, precision-guided therapy.
companies.problem: Sepsis the body’s extreme response to infection is responsible for around 11 million deaths annually worldwide and is linked to 1 in 3 hospital deaths in the U.S. Early symptoms (like fever or confusion) are vague, and traditional blood cultures are slow and often miss infections leaving clinicians blind and patients at risk.
companies.description: DeepUll’s UllCORE platform delivers culture-free, direct-from-blood sepsis diagnostics identifying pathogens, resistance genes, and treatment guidance within hours instead of days.

companies.name: DeHaat
companies.one_liner: What if, we build a digital platform to help small-scale farmers grow their businesses?

companies.name: Delfos Energy
companies.one_liner: Finds the power a wind farm never made.
companies.solution: Getting more clean power from the turbines and panels already standing is one of the fastest wins in the energy transition. Small gains at each site add up to a lot of extra clean electricity, without new land or construction. It arrives with no permits to win and nothing to build, in the very years when new projects sit waiting in a connection queue, and the view from the nearest village stays exactly as it was.
companies.problem: Wind, solar, hydro and battery sites produce huge amounts of data, but engineers don't have time to read it all, so sites quietly underproduce for months, and faults go unnoticed until they break something. Delfos Energy uses AI to analyse this data and gives operators a clear list of what to fix, when, and what it will cost if they wait. The signals already stream in from each manufacturer's own system, and the ranking pulls the real fault out from under the nuisance alerts.

companies.name: Dendra Systems
companies.one_liner: Planting seeds using drones to rebuild and restore rainforests.

companies.name: Desolenator
companies.one_liner: What if, poor communities could use the sun to make their own freshwater at scale?

companies.name: Dioxycle
companies.one_liner: Turns factory smoke into plastic.
companies.solution: Imagine a steel mill or cement plant turning its own smoke into something it can sell. That would change how and where chemicals are made: smaller, cleaner and right next to the factories whose waste becomes the raw material. Chemical making would sit in the towns built around heavy industry, rather than out by the ports where fossil feedstock arrives, and the air those towns breathe would carry less of the works.
companies.problem: Plastics start with a chemical called ethylene, made today in huge fossil-fuel plants that run at around eight hundred degrees. Dioxycle is building cells that use electricity and water to turn the carbon in factory exhaust into ethylene and other everyday chemicals instead. They are designed to work at ordinary temperatures, taking carbon monoxide or carbon dioxide from a furnace's exhaust and giving back ethylene, or formic acid.
companies.description: Dioxycle uses low-cost renewable electricity to power electrochemical reactors that convert CO₂ into valuable products like synthetic fuels and chemicals. Their breakthrough tech creates a closed-loop carbon economy capturing emissions at the source and turning them into clean, circular commodities.

companies.name: Djamo
companies.one_liner: The unbanked, now carrying a full bank
companies.solution: If everyday people can save, borrow and invest from their phones, they gain tools to plan for the future, handle emergencies and grow their businesses. That could help millions build financial security across West Africa, in places where a branch has never been within easy reach. For a market trader or a young worker sending money home, it is the difference between money that only moves and money that can also grow.
companies.problem: In Francophone West Africa, most adults don't have a bank account, and mobile money lets people send money but not save or borrow. Djamo offers a banking app with a card, interest-earning savings, small loans and even access to the regional stock market. A customer signs up from a phone and gets an account number and a Visa card, without the payslips and proof of address a branch would ask for and cannot get from informal earners.

companies.name: Dunia Innovations
companies.one_liner: Dunia compresses decades of clean-energy material discovery breakthroughs into just years, supercharging discovery with AI and robotics.
companies.solution: Dunia combines cutting-edge AI algorithms with a proprietary self-driving lab to revolutionise the discovery of advanced materials, focused on designing catalysts for green hydrogen and ammonia production, and converting CO2 into higher-value chemical products.
companies.problem: Traditional development of electroactive materials, vital for clean energy, like catalysts for green hydrogen or CO₂ conversion, takes decades and costs too much .
companies.description: Dunia’s autonomous “self-driving lab” combines physics-informed AI with robotic automation to run closed-loop design–make–test–analyze cycles, discovering breakthrough electroactive materials up to 10× faster and at a third of the cost .

companies.name: Eat Just
companies.one_liner: What If, We Could Have Both Eggs And Chicken Without Any Real Chickens?

companies.name: Ebb Carbon
companies.one_liner: Using oceans to capture carbon from the air.

companies.name: Ecording
companies.one_liner: What if, we use drones to help birds spread seeds around the world?

companies.name: Ecoworks
companies.one_liner: Factory-built solutions that make old houses far more energy efficient.

companies.name: eFishery
companies.one_liner: Ending hunger by improving shrimp farming.

companies.name: Einride
companies.one_liner: Putting the world's first electric and self-driving trucks on roads everywhere.

companies.name: Electricity Maps
companies.one_liner: Tracking your electricity’s carbon footprint in real-time.

companies.name: Ellipsis Health
companies.one_liner: Using voice analysis to detect early mental health symptoms.

companies.name: Elonroad
companies.one_liner: What if, we build roads that charge electric vehicles as they go?

companies.name: Elyos Energy
companies.one_liner: Teaching buildings to use less energy with smart tech that learns how to save power.

companies.name: Endolith
companies.one_liner: Microbes unlock the copper conventional mining leaves behind
companies.solution: If microbes can release copper from rock that's currently discarded, existing mines could produce more without digging new pits. That could help meet the growing demand for copper for electric cars, grids and renewables, with less environmental disruption. For the communities living beside a working mine, more of the metal comes from ground already opened up, rather than from somewhere new having to be broken open.
companies.problem: The most common type of copper ore is hard to process, so much low-grade rock is left on waste piles at mines. Endolith uses tailored teams of microbes, chosen with the help of software for each site, to release copper from ore on existing processing pads. The microbes free the copper into the liquid running through the heap, on pads a mine has already built, so rock written off as too poor to treat could go back into production.

companies.name: Enerdrape
companies.one_liner: Turning underground spaces into hidden power sources by capturing geothermal and wasted heat.

companies.name: Enerin
companies.one_liner: A fridge run backwards, making steam.
companies.solution: Most heat pumps can't get hot enough for heavy industry, which is why factories still burn fuel and keep a stack running whenever the line runs. Enerin's approach could make it practical for paper mills, distilleries and chemical plants to switch to clean electric heat. The warm water a plant has always poured away would come back as the heat the work needs, and the towns built around those mills would keep the mill and lose the chimney.
companies.problem: Factories use huge amounts of heat for drying, distilling and sterilising, mostly from gas-fired boilers, while warm water from the process is thrown away. Enerin's heat pump uses helium to capture that waste heat and boost it to the high temperatures industrial processes need, running on electricity. Compressing and expanding helium rather than boiling a refrigerant lets it reach hot water, steam or thermal oil in one step, and give back chilled water at the cold end.

companies.name: EnginZyme
companies.one_liner: Reducing chemical production waste by replacing heavy metals with enzymes to create net-zero products.

companies.name: Enline
companies.one_liner: Software that makes power lines bigger.
companies.solution: Many clean energy projects wait years for grid connections. If existing lines can safely carry more power, some of those projects could connect much sooner, making better use of the grid we already have. It would mean more clean electricity travelling on wires already strung across the country, with no new towers and no new land, and towns waiting on a wind farm getting their power years earlier than the queue would ever have allowed.
companies.problem: Power lines are rated as if it's always a hot, windless, sunny day, which means they often carry far less electricity than they safely could. Enline uses a digital model of the grid, combining weather, terrain and line data, to calculate how much power each line can really carry at any moment. Because nothing has to be fitted to a live conductor, a whole network can be rated this way rather than one circuit at a time.

companies.name: Enter
companies.one_liner: Helps you monitor energy consumptions and finance your upgrade to cleaner energy.

companies.name: Entrix
companies.one_liner: Stores and trades surplus power so none of it goes to waste
companies.solution: If battery owners can count on steady income, banks will be more willing to finance new storage projects, and more of them will clear the credit committee. More batteries on the grid means less clean power wasted and a smoother path to a renewable energy system. For the rest of us, it means the wind that blows hard on a quiet night is still worth something by morning, instead of being turned away.
companies.problem: Large batteries help store surplus wind and solar power, but earning money from them means trading electricity around the clock across complex markets. Entrix runs grid batteries it does not own using automated trading software that decides minute by minute whether to charge, hold or sell, bidding the same battery into several European markets at once. Owners get the benefit without staffing a trading desk of their own.

companies.name: Epoch Biodesign
companies.one_liner: Landfill nylon becomes new fiber
companies.solution: If enzymes can recycle mixed and coated nylon, old garments and car fabrics could become the raw material for new products, rather than something someone pays to get rid of. That would give nylon waste real value and help cut the need for oil-based production. It would also give the people who collect and sort textiles a reason to keep nylon aside and handle it with care, because somebody is waiting to buy it.
companies.problem: Nylon in clothing, airbags and car interiors is very hard to recycle, because coatings, dyes and stretchy blends defeat shredding, so most of it ends up in landfill or is burned, while new nylon is made from oil. Epoch Biodesign uses AI to design enzymes that break nylon down into its basic building blocks in water, at room temperature rather than furnace heat. Worn clothing and old airbag fabric can become the material they started as.

companies.name: Epyr
companies.one_liner: Turning renewable power into high-temperature heat with thermal energy storage
companies.solution: converting renewable electricity into heat during low-cost energy periods and storing it in high-efficiency firebricks, in doing so delivering high-temperature, decarbonized heat to industries while easing the burden on the power grid and supporting the energy transition
companies.problem: Industrial heat accounts for 25% of global energy consumption.  Today, most of this heat is generated from fossil fuels like natural gas, oil, and coal.
companies.description: Epyr builds modular heat storage systems stores sustainable produced heat and convert it into usable power or steam. Their plug-and-play tech integrates easily with existing plants, cutting emissions and costs without overhauling infrastructure making industrial decarbonization both fast and profitable.

companies.name: Esusu
companies.one_liner: What if, tenants could build credit score by being on time with rent payments?

companies.name: Etalytics
companies.one_liner: Teaches data centres to cool themselves.
companies.solution: Data centres are one of the fastest-growing users of electricity, and new ones wait years in the queue for a grid connection. If smart software can cut their cooling needs without new equipment, grids gain precious capacity and the digital world grows with a smaller footprint. No new power line, no new permit, nothing built: only the buildings that already stand, asking a little less of the towns around them.
companies.problem: Data centres use a lot of energy just to stay cool, and their cooling systems often run on settings chosen the day they were switched on, with plenty of waste built in. Etalytics creates a digital model of a site's cooling system, combining the physics of the plant with its own sensor history, then uses AI to adjust it constantly based on weather, workload and electricity prices. The site might be a data centre, a car plant or a pharmaceutical works.

companies.name: EveryDay Labs
companies.one_liner: Ensuring children's engagement and happiness in school by utilizing data analysis to monitor health and attendance.

companies.name: Evroc
companies.one_liner: A cloud Europe owns, not one it rents
companies.solution: A strong European cloud would give organisations real choice over where their data lives and whose rules apply, so a hospital could run its work without accepting another country's courts over it. That could help Europe build its digital future on infrastructure it owns and shapes itself. Sovereignty would stop being a clause buried in a contract and become an ordinary choice, settled close to home by the people it concerns.
companies.problem: European banks, hospitals and governments that want advanced cloud and AI services mostly have to use American providers, which puts their data under foreign law. Evroc is building a full European cloud platform from the ground up, writing its own software and building its own data centres in Sweden and France. It serves customers today from leased halls in Stockholm, Paris and Frankfurt while those sites go up.
companies.description: EVROC is building a European hyperscale cloud platform powered 100% by renewable energy. With local data centers and open, secure infrastructure, they’re giving Europe control over its digital future while slashing emissions from the data economy.

companies.name: Exergy3
companies.one_liner: Factory heat, made from wasted power.
companies.solution: If surplus wind power can be stored as heat, distilleries, food plants and glassworks could run on clean energy that would otherwise go to waste, buying it in the hours it costs least. It turns a grid problem into an industrial one that can be solved. The power that Scottish wind farms are now paid to stop making would end up in the whisky, the bread and the window glass instead, in towns that live beside the turbines.
companies.problem: Factories need high-temperature heat on demand, usually from gas, even when wind farms are being paid to switch off because there's too much power. Exergy3 builds modular thermal storage that soaks up cheap surplus electricity in short bursts and stores it as heat far above what a boiler or heat pump reaches, releasing it as a controlled stream of hot gas whenever the factory needs it. A distillery can take its heat from the windiest hour of the week.

companies.name: Exponent Energy
companies.one_liner: Delivers 15-minute EV charging.
companies.solution: Exponent Energy focuses on developing fast charging technology for electric vehicles.
companies.problem: Electric vehicle adoption is booming but slow charging and unreliable infrastructure make it hard for fleet operators and commercial drivers to switch from fossil fuels.
companies.description: Exponent Energy builds battery packs and charging stations designed for ultra-fast charging in tough conditions. Their unique battery-tech combo enables 15-minute top-ups without overheating or grid stress making electrification practical and profitable.

companies.name: Fabric Nano
companies.one_liner: Crafting the future of biochemistry without living cells.

companies.name: Faircado
companies.one_liner: Searches through all of second-hand sources using AI.
companies.solution: Faircado makes online shopping for secondhand items easier through its free, AI-powered browser extension that’s designed to point online shoppers to used options when they’re searching for new ones.
companies.problem: Online shopping drives overproduction, waste, and emissions, yet most consumers still default to buying new because finding quality secondhand items is fragmented, time-consuming, and buried in obscure platforms.
companies.description: Faircado makes online shopping for secondhand items easier through its free, AI-powered browser extension that’s designed to point online shoppers to used options when they’re searching for new ones.

companies.name: Farmforce
companies.one_liner: What if, we build a digital platform to help small farmers access large markets?

companies.name: FarmHQ
companies.one_liner: What if, we could save water by retrofitting old farmland equipment with internet connectivity?

companies.name: Farmless
companies.one_liner: Brews protein out of thin air and electricity.
companies.solution: If protein can be made from air and electricity at a competitive price, food production could be freed from its dependence on land. That could ease pressure on forests and farmland, and let protein be produced almost anywhere in the world. The world's protein map has always followed its farmland map, and a tank that runs on carbon and electricity is one of the few things that could begin to draw that map differently.
companies.problem: All our protein, whether from animals, soy or peas, depends on farmland, and so do the fermented alternatives, which are fed on sugar that is grown in fields as well. Farmless makes protein without fields: microbes in an ordinary brewing tank feed on an ingredient made from captured carbon, hydrogen and renewable electricity, producing a complete protein powder. What the tank needs is electricity and volume, not hectares.

companies.name: FarmWorks
companies.one_liner: Turns Kenya’s food system into a resilient, high-tech ecosystem, where underutilized land, trained farmers, smart farms, and stable markets work together to feed a nation.
companies.solution: FarmWorks is a Kenyan agritech company that empowers smallholder farmers through a vertically integrated model combining inputs, training, and market access.
companies.problem: Millions of Kenyan farmers lack access to finance, inputs, training, and reliable markets while fresh food supply chains remain fragmented and inconsistent.
companies.description: FarmWorks builds an integrated agri-food ecosystem, supporting climate-smart farms, training apprentices through its Institute, providing inputs and market access, and using tech to reduce waste and stabilize prices.

companies.name: Fervo Energy
companies.one_liner: Leveraging oil and gas drilling technology to produce clean geothermal energy at scale.

companies.name: Fleetzero
companies.one_liner: No diesel left in a cargo ship's tank
companies.solution: If large ships can run much of their time on batteries, shipping emissions could fall on today's vessels, without waiting for new fuels. It could also mean cleaner air in ports and coastal cities where ships spend hours with engines running. For people who live beside a working harbour, that change arrives at the window rather than in a report, on the morning a ship comes in quiet and the air by the quayside smells of the sea.
companies.problem: Ships run almost entirely on heavy fuel oil or diesel, and large marine batteries are hard to get, with long lead times and few suppliers to order from. Fleetzero builds container-sized battery systems for ships, along with the power hub that ties them into the propulsion, so vessels can run on stored electricity for part of their journeys and on their engines for the rest. The modules go into new ships and into ones already at sea.
companies.description: Fleetzero designs and operates fully electric cargo ships powered by swappable battery packs. Their modular, no-fuel-needed approach decarbonizes freight at sea, dramatically cutting emissions while reducing operating costs and creating a cleaner, quieter maritime future.

companies.name: Flok Health
companies.one_liner: Treats back and joint pain without a waiting list
companies.solution: If routine cases can be treated without a waiting list, more people get help sooner, and physiotherapists can focus on patients with more complex needs. It could be a new model for making healthcare capacity grow with demand, rather than with the number of people a service manages to hire. For someone whose back has hurt since spring, it means getting back to the stairs, the garden and the ordinary day that much sooner.
companies.problem: Back and joint pain is one of the biggest causes of disability worldwide, and patients often wait months for physiotherapy, because every appointment takes a clinician's hour. Flok offers physio through video appointments led by an AI clinician that assesses patients, sets exercises and adjusts treatment at each follow-up, handing over to a human physio when needed. Treatment can begin in days rather than seasons.

companies.name: Floodbase
companies.one_liner: Flood claims from orbit
companies.solution: With reliable flood maps from space, insurance can reach communities and regions that insurers have never been able to serve, in places where no adjuster network has ever operated. Farmers, small businesses and governments could get money fast after a disaster, when it matters most for recovery. Money that arrives in days pays for the seed, the repair and the reopening while there is still something to save.
companies.problem: Most flood damage worldwide is uninsured, partly because checking every claim in person is slow and costly, with an adjuster visiting each site and the paperwork running for months. Floodbase combines satellite images, river data and modelling to map exactly where a flood hit and how far the water spread, so insurers can pay out quickly when a flood reaches a set level. Nobody has to photograph a ruined room to prove it.

companies.name: Flower
companies.one_liner: Brings stability and balance to the energy system with a virtual power plant.

companies.name: Flox Intelligence
companies.one_liner: Talk to animals before conflict starts
companies.solution: If technology can keep deer, moose and birds away safely, fewer animals would need to be shot and fewer collisions would happen on rails, runways and roads. It points to a future where people and wildlife share space with less conflict. A field, a railway line and the animals that cross it could each carry on much as before, with the warning arriving in a language the animals already know and keep listening to.
companies.problem: Animals near airports, railways and farms cause collisions and crop damage, and keeping them away usually means people on patrol, loud cannons or culling. Flox places a smart device on site that works out which animal is there, on the device itself, and plays back calls from that animal's own species, varied so they don't get used to them. It sits on a battery beside a runway, a track or a field, with nobody there.

companies.name: FluxGen Tech
companies.one_liner: Turns every drop of water into data, slashes waste and boosts energy efficiency.

companies.name: Foray
companies.one_liner: What If, We Grow Wood In A Lab Instead Of Cutting Down Trees?

companies.name: Form Energy
companies.one_liner: What if, we could rust and de-rust iron to store energy cheaply and at scale?

companies.name: Formo
companies.one_liner: Making delicious cheese using microorganisms instead of cows.

companies.name: Found Industries
companies.one_liner: Scrap metal releases clean heat
companies.solution: Waste metal could become a clean fuel that arrives by truck and stores energy on site for days. For factories far from cheap power, that could offer a practical way off gas, using materials that would otherwise leave as low-value scrap. Energy would no longer have to reach a place by pipe or wire to be useful there, which matters most in towns built around a plant that has run on gas for as long as anyone remembers.
companies.problem: Factories that use gas to make steam can't easily switch to electricity without replacing their boilers and getting a bigger grid connection. Found Industries coats scrap aluminium with a liquid alloy so it reacts with water, releasing heat and hydrogen that can feed straight into a factory's existing steam system. The boiler and the pipework stay where they are, and the scrap can be the plant's own offcuts, which today leave for a remelter that pays little for them.

companies.name: Galvany
companies.one_liner: Retrofits the buildings solar companies skip
companies.solution: If one company can take care of everything, many more older buildings could move off gas faster. Smart control also lets homes use electricity when it's plentiful, easing pressure on the grid and lowering bills. For a family in an older apartment, the change would arrive simply as a warm home and a smaller bill at the end of the month, without anyone in the building having to become an expert in heating to get there.
companies.problem: Switching from a gas boiler to a heat pump means finding an installer, applying for subsidies and hoping the system runs well, and nobody keeps an eye on it once it's fitted. Galvany handles the whole process, from the sale through to installers it manages end to end, then runs the system to heat homes when electricity is cheapest. A control box shifts heating and hot water into the cheaper hours, so the company stays responsible long after the invoice is paid.

companies.name: Galy
companies.one_liner: Creating ethical and sustainable cotton from start to finish - in labs.

companies.name: Genomines
companies.one_liner: Plants extract metals the earth can't reach
companies.solution: Imagine farming metals instead of digging for them. If plant-based mining works at scale, battery materials could come from degraded land in months rather than from new open pits after years, giving the energy transition a gentler way to source what it needs. For the places where this metal sits near the surface, that could mean a growing season and a harvest rather than a haul road and a tailings pond.
companies.problem: Batteries need nickel, but new nickel mines take over a decade to open, cost billions and can damage forests. Genomines grows engineered plants that draw nickel up out of the soil. After a few months the leaves are harvested and processed into battery-grade nickel. The plants grow on nickel-bearing ground too thin to justify a pit, a haul fleet and a smelter, and the crop can come round again the following season.

companies.name: Gigmile
companies.one_liner: Grows vehicle owners out of gig drivers
companies.solution: If this model spreads across West Africa, millions of gig drivers could end up owning the vehicles they work with. Ownership builds a foundation for financial security, turning a daily hustle into an asset that belongs to the driver. A vehicle that is finally paid off is also something a family can borrow against, lend to a relative, hand on to someone else, or use to start a second line of work of their own.
companies.problem: Many ride-hail and delivery drivers in Nigeria can't get a bank loan, so they rent vehicles on tough terms and may never own them. Gigmile leases motorbikes, tricycles and cars on a rent-to-own basis, with payments based on what drivers actually earn and insurance and servicing included. The payment is sized against trip and earnings data from the platforms a driver already works on, and at the end of the term the vehicle is theirs to keep.
companies.description: Gigmile provides mobility-focused gig workers with affordable rent-to-own financing, asset subscriptions, and micro-loans empowering them to earn, grow, and participate anywhere they work.

companies.name: Goodfire AI
companies.one_liner: Critical infrastructure to edit and control AI before it controls us.
