companies.solution: allows researchers to examine the internal workings of large language models with proprietary tool that makes LLMs interpretable, ensuring powerful systems behave as intended in various applications
companies.problem: Current AI model training is black-box: we throw in data and hope they learn what we want. This can lead to unexpected, unwanted, at times harmful behaviors. With rapidly evolving models, interpretability is urgent.
companies.description: Goodfire AI advances humanity's understanding of AI by examining the inner workings of advanced AI models (AI interpretability) - empowering developers to understand, edit, and debug AI models at scale, ensuring the creation of safer and more reliable systems.

companies.name: Goterra
companies.one_liner: Uses maggots and robots to turn food waste into high quality soil.
companies.solution: Revolutionizes waste management by deploying maggots filled robots that process organic waste onsite.
companies.problem: Food waste is a massive climate and resource problem—emitting methane in landfills, costing billions, and squandering nutrients that could regenerate soil. Traditional waste management is centralized, inefficient, and carbon-heavy.
companies.description: Goterra deploys modular, automated insect farms that process food waste on-site using black soldier fly larvae. Their tech reduces waste volume by 90%, produces high-quality protein and compost, and turns organic waste into a local circular economy asset.

companies.name: Granular Energy
companies.one_liner: 24/7 clean energy trading and management.

companies.name: Greenjoules
companies.one_liner: Makes renewable biofuels from agricultural waste with zero fossil fuels involved.
companies.solution: Green Joules produces second-generation biofuels from agricultural waste, offering sustainable fuel alternatives compatible with existing diesel infrastructure
companies.problem: India’s transport and industrial sectors are heavily reliant on fossil diesel, contributing to both urban air pollution and global climate emissions. Meanwhile, agricultural residues are burned, causing environmental damage and wasted potential.
companies.description: Greenjoules produces drop-in green diesel from agricultural and industrial waste using proprietary technology. Their fuel is fossil-free, cleaner-burning, and compatible with existing engines—empowering industries and heavy vehicles to decarbonize without changing infrastructure.

companies.name: Greenlyte Carbon Technologies
companies.one_liner: Cutting-edge carbon capture and conversion.

companies.name: GreyParrot
companies.one_liner: Uses AI to see, and sort, what humans miss in waste.
companies.solution: applying AI to globally scale recycling and save millions of tonnes of waste from landfills and incinerators
companies.problem: Over 80% of the world’s waste is not properly sorted, making recycling inefficient, expensive, and largely ineffective. Most waste facilities operate blind, with no real-time data on what passes through their systems.
companies.description: Greyparrot installs AI-powered cameras and software in waste facilities to identify, track, and categorize waste at scale. Their system provides live insights and automates sorting decisions—turning chaotic waste streams into measurable, high-value recycling flows.

companies.name: Gridware
companies.one_liner: Feels a power line fail.
companies.solution: If utilities know exactly where a problem is, a crew goes straight to the span instead of patrolling miles of line to find it. That could mean fewer wildfires, fewer blackouts and a safer, smarter grid. On a windy day in a dry town, that is the difference between a crew sent out to one span of wire and a whole valley sitting in the dark, with fridges warming and phones going flat, waiting for the wind to drop.
companies.problem: Power companies often only learn a line has failed when a customer calls or smoke appears, and faults can spark wildfires. Gridware attaches solar-powered sensors to power poles that detect problems like a fallen branch, a broken wire or a leaning pole the moment they happen. Each sensor listens to the wire and the pole itself, tracking vibration, sound and tilt, and works out on the spot which of those has gone wrong.
companies.description: Gridware builds rugged, AI-enabled sensors that mount directly to power poles and monitor grid health in real time. They detect faults, sparks, and vibrations instantly—giving utilities a live map of grid safety and helping prevent disaster before it starts.

companies.name: H2Pro
companies.one_liner: Making sustainable green hydrogen fuel as affordable as fossil fuels.

companies.name: H2SITE
companies.one_liner: Bringing renewable hydrogen right to your doorstep, fueling small and medium businesses with clean energy.

companies.name: Hades Mining
companies.one_liner: Laser drilling unlocks Europe's minerals
companies.solution: If lasers can drill deep and fast, the heat beneath our feet becomes accessible across much of Europe, and so do minerals that clean technologies depend on. Deep geothermal energy and local supply of critical metals could become realistic almost anywhere. A city could then draw its winter warmth from the hot rock directly underneath it, rather than from something shipped in from the other side of the world.
companies.problem: Drilling deep into hard rock is slow and expensive: drill bits wear out and have to be pulled all the way up to be replaced. Hades Mining uses a powerful laser, sent down through optical fibre, to break rock without any mechanical cutter touching it. The heat cracks the rock at the bottom of the hole while jets of high-pressure fluid clear the fragments away, so there is no bit to blunt and nothing to haul up and change.

companies.name: Heart Aerospace
companies.one_liner: Designs electric planes that use batteries, cutting emissions to nearly zero.

companies.name: Heirloom
companies.one_liner: Uses natural minerals to capture CO2 from the air -and permanently storing it.

companies.name: Helios Innovations
companies.one_liner: Uses waste heat to clean industrial wastewater on-site
companies.solution: If only the concentrated waste needs to travel, existing treatment facilities could handle pollution from far more sites. That could help clean up forever chemicals faster and protect drinking water for communities everywhere. It would also mean fewer tankers of mostly water on the road, and more places able to deal with what they have made close to where they made it, instead of sending it across a country and waiting in the queue.
companies.problem: Factories with water polluted by PFAS, the 'forever chemicals', usually have to truck all of it to a handful of specialist incinerators, even though it's mostly water. Helios places a compact unit on site that evaporates the water at low temperatures, leaving the pollutants behind in a much smaller residue. The water trickles over cellulose blocks that spread it thin enough to evaporate gently, and the vapour condenses clean enough to reuse.

companies.name: Hertha Metals
companies.one_liner: Clean steel from dirty ore
companies.solution: If lower-grade ore and waste can become high-quality iron, steelmaking could get cleaner and more local. Resources that end up in landfill today could supply key industries, from magnets to machines. Ore a country already has, and the waste already sitting in heaps beside its mills, could become the starting point for the metal its industries need, rather than something bought on a long line that runs halfway around the world.
companies.problem: Traditional steelmaking relies on coal and high-grade iron ore, and some specialised high-purity iron has to be imported. Hertha Metals has developed a single furnace that turns iron ore, including low-grade ore and steel plant waste, into high-purity iron using natural gas or hydrogen instead of coal. One continuous reactor does the work of a coke oven, a blast furnace and a separate refining step, drawing off liquid metal pure enough for magnet makers.

companies.name: Hive Health
companies.one_liner: Brings real health coverage to small business staff
companies.solution: If small employers can offer real health cover, millions more workers could get care without fear of the bill. A serious illness wouldn't have to wipe out a family's savings, and small businesses could compete for talent with bigger ones. For the family of someone working in a small shop or a small office, a week in hospital would stop being the thing that quietly undoes years of careful saving, or sends a household to a lender to cover the rest.
companies.problem: In the Philippines, most small businesses can't offer staff health insurance, so employees pay much of their hospital bills from savings or loans. Hive Health offers group health plans for companies with as few as three employees, with everything from sign-up to claims handled in a simple app. Staff can be added or removed within a business day, and members use the app to find accredited providers, book teleconsultations and file claims.

companies.name: Hived
companies.one_liner: Planet-first parcel delivery.

companies.name: HoneyCoin
companies.one_liner: African payments, minus the US detour
companies.solution: If paying a supplier across a border becomes as fast and cheap as paying one across town, African businesses could trade far more with each other. That could help regional trade grow and keep more value inside the continent. A trader buying from a workshop in the country next door could send the money in the morning and expect it to arrive before the day is out, and plan the next order around that rather than around the wait.
companies.problem: Sending a business payment from one African country to another often means routing money through US dollars or euros, which adds cost and can take days. HoneyCoin moves money between African currencies directly, using digital dollars behind the scenes and paying out through local banks and mobile money. The money lands in a local account or a mobile wallet at the far end, without either side keeping a dollar account open.

companies.name: Hydroleap
companies.one_liner: Cleaning water with tech that’s as green as it gets.

companies.name: Hyfé
companies.one_liner: Turns food waste into sustainable chemicals.

companies.name: Idoven
companies.one_liner: Preventing heart attacks using AI.

companies.name: Inbrain
companies.one_liner: Uses AI-powered neural interfaces to treat brain disorders and unlock a new era of healthcare.

companies.name: Infinited Fiber
companies.one_liner: What if, we made all our new clothes from old clothes?

companies.name: Innovafeed
companies.one_liner: Enabling more food for a growing population with sustainable, insect-based animal feed.

companies.name: Instagrid
companies.one_liner: What if, we replace portable diesel generators with portable batteries?

companies.name: Intramotev
companies.one_liner: Electrifies freight one wagon at a time
companies.solution: If wagons can move on their own, short rail trips could become cheap and flexible again. Some of the freight now carried by trucks could return to rail, cutting emissions and congestion on the roads. For the towns and villages strung along those routes, that means fewer lorries passing the school gates, quieter streets and cleaner air, and a little more room on the roads for everyone who still needs to use them.
companies.problem: Moving a few freight wagons a short distance by rail isn't worth the cost of a locomotive and crew, so that freight often goes by truck instead. Intramotev fits standard freight wagons with battery-electric drives so they can move themselves, singly or in small groups. A plant that needs to shift a couple of loaded cars a mile or two can send them on their own, instead of keeping a diesel switcher idling on site or paying a contract crew by the hour.

companies.name: IONATE
companies.one_liner: More power through the same old wires.
companies.solution: Smarter transformers could let existing grids take on far more clean energy and new connections without digging up streets. That means households and businesses could connect sooner, and grid upgrades could go where they're truly needed. For a family waiting to plug in a heat pump, or a workshop waiting to switch on its own rooftop solar, it is the difference between a wait measured in years and one measured in weeks.
companies.problem: The transformers on our streets were built decades ago and weren't designed for today's solar panels, electric cars and heat pumps, so many new connections are delayed or refused. IONATE builds smart transformers that can actively manage voltage and power flow, fitting in the same space as conventional ones. Because the electronics sit alongside the iron core rather than replacing it, one unit can steady the voltage on each phase, steer power where it is needed and report what it sees.

companies.name: Isometric
companies.one_liner: Proves that carbon really left the air.
companies.solution: Checking carbon removal is currently slow and expensive, so only big projects can afford it. If rigorous verification gets faster and cheaper, a single farm or small plant could sell trusted carbon removal too, opening the market to many more of the people doing the actual work. A farmer spreading crushed rock across a field, or a village kiln turning waste into charcoal, could be counted alongside the largest projects.
companies.problem: Carbon credits have a trust problem: in the old model, sellers pay for their own audits, and many credits have turned out not to represent real reductions. Isometric writes strict scientific standards for each type of carbon removal, uses software to check the evidence, and makes the data behind every credit public. Buyers pay, not sellers. Each standard sets out exactly what evidence a method must produce, software reads most of it, and the harder cases go to people.

companies.name: Jua
companies.one_liner: Predicts weather to keep clean power flowing
companies.solution: Accurate, affordable forecasts would let smaller grid operators and renewable energy companies plan as well as the biggest players. Better planning means less waste, steadier grids and more room for clean energy in the system. And for the households and towns drawing on those grids, it means the lights hold steady on a still, grey day, with less of the guesswork that somebody always ends up paying for.
companies.problem: Wind and solar traders need precise, up-to-the-minute weather forecasts for each site, but public forecasts arrive a few times a day and cover big areas. Jua's AI produces detailed wind, sunlight and temperature forecasts that update constantly, without needing a supercomputer. Instead of buying a regional forecast and paying meteorologists to narrow it down to a single wind farm by hand, a desk can see the ridge and the valley apart.

companies.name: Juli
companies.one_liner: What if, AI could help patients self-manage their chronic health conditions?

companies.name: Juna AI
companies.one_liner: Teaches a factory to save its own energy
companies.solution: Imagine every cement, glass and paper plant learning from the others, so a lesson from one kiln helps the next. Energy efficiency would stop being a one-off project at each site and start building on itself across whole industries, cutting fuel use and emissions as it goes. The materials a town is built from, its cement, its glass, its paper, would quietly get cheaper to make and lighter on the air around them.
companies.problem: Big industrial plants burn more energy than they need to, because furnaces and boilers slowly drift away from their best settings and engineers can't watch every one around the clock. Juna's AI agents read the plant's own data, spot the drift early and suggest a fix, with an operator signing off before anything changes. The agents follow how heat and material move through the plant, catching the small, steady losses that a trend screen misses between reviews.
companies.description: Juna AI optimizes energy-intensive production processes with AI-based control and scheduling. Their customized co-pilots are trained on historical process data and increase resource efficiency, throughput and utilization of industrial plants.

companies.name: Kapu
companies.one_liner: Making food in Africa more affordable.

companies.name: Karius
companies.one_liner: What if, we apply AI to blood samples to detect almost every human pathogen?

companies.name: Kitekraft
companies.one_liner: Building flying wind turbines to get wind powered energy more efficiently.

companies.name: Klim
companies.one_liner: Paying farmers to heal soil and pull carbon from the sky.
companies.solution: Klim supports farmers and companies in the transition to regenerative agriculture
companies.problem: Conventional agriculture depletes soil health, emits greenhouse gases, and contributes to biodiversity loss. Yet farmers often lack the incentives, knowledge, or support to transition to regenerative practices that restore ecosystems and sequester carbon.
companies.description: Klim offers a digital platform that guides farmers through regenerative practices and connects them to carbon credit buyers. By monetizing soil restoration, Klim unlocks a scalable path to climate-positive farming. Backed by science, verified impact, and empowered growers.

companies.name: KoBoldMetals
companies.one_liner: Digitally hunting for cobalt with machine prospector tech (read with terminator voice).

companies.name: Koolboks
companies.one_liner: Freezers that keep working after dark.
companies.solution: Reliable cooling changes what a small business can sell, from fish to dairy. If solar freezers spread like solar home systems did, food waste could fall, incomes rise and whole neighbourhoods gain access to fresher food. Street by street, it would show up as a wider choice on the stalls people already shop at, and as a trader whose working day no longer begins with carrying home a block of ice bought before dawn.
companies.problem: Many market traders in Nigeria can't keep food cold without buying ice every day or running costly petrol generators, so unsold stock often spoils. Koolboks makes solar-powered freezers that store energy in ice and batteries to stay cold overnight and through cloudy days, with payments spread over time. That means no ice seller to visit before dawn and no fuel to price into every sale, and stock that can wait for a buyer.

companies.name: Kraftblock
companies.one_liner: Stores solar energy from summertime to make wintertime more affordable (and warmer).

companies.name: Kwara
companies.one_liner: What if, we give the world's poor access to modern digital banking?

companies.name: Lanza Jet
companies.one_liner: Makes circular jet fuel from waste, cutting aviation emissions
companies.solution: Leading the Charge in Sustainable Aviation Fuel innovation with the world's first and only Alcohol-to-Jet facility
companies.problem: Aviation is one of the fastest-growing sources of carbon emissions, and traditional fossil-based jet fuel is difficult to replace. Most alternatives are either too expensive, incompatible with existing engines, or limited in supply.
companies.description: LanzaJet produces sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) from waste-based ethanol using a patented alcohol-to-jet process. Their fuel is drop-in ready, dramatically reduces lifecycle emissions, and works in today’s aircraft, helping decarbonize aviation without waiting for new planes or policies.

companies.name: Lilac Solutions
companies.one_liner: Extracting lithium for batteries from natural salt water deposits.

companies.name: Living Carbon
companies.one_liner: Combating climate change by making trees into the ultimate CO2 storage units.

companies.name: Luxwall
companies.one_liner: Making vacuum-insulated glass windows, cutting carbon emissions by half a gigatonne annually.

companies.name: Made of Air
companies.one_liner: What if, we make clothes that reverse climate change?

companies.name: Magnotherm
companies.one_liner: Cools down our planet with new magnetic cooling technology.

companies.name: Mainspring Energy
companies.one_liner: Paving the way for a future green energy grid by creating generators that operate on multiple clean energy sources.

companies.name: Makersite
companies.one_liner: Uses deep-tier supply chain data to help businesses create sustainable products without the guesswork.

companies.name: Mamotest
companies.one_liner: What if, we do mammography over the internet for women in poor communities?

companies.name: Mango Materials
companies.one_liner: Making plastics biodegradable through waste biogas.

companies.name: Mantle8
companies.one_liner: Clean fuel the Earth already made.
companies.solution: Almost all hydrogen today has to be manufactured, using gas or lots of electricity. Hydrogen straight from the ground could give Europe's heavy industry a clean fuel it doesn't need to build a factory to produce. Priced more like a mineral than a product, it would be something a country finds under its own hills, the way it once found coal or water, rather than something it has to build a plant to make.
companies.problem: Deep underground, some rocks make hydrogen naturally when they meet water. Finding it is hard, because the tools we have were built to hunt for oil. Mantle8 combines several kinds of geological data into one model that shows where natural hydrogen is being made, where it moves and where it gets trapped. Oil sits still and waits to be found; this is a small, restless gas that leaks through seals and reacts with rock on its way up.

companies.name: Material Evolution
companies.one_liner: Makes ultra-low carbon cement from industrial waste.
companies.solution: Material Evolution develops ultra-low carbon cement using proprietary Alkali Fusion technology and AI-driven material optimization.
companies.problem: Cement is responsible for 8% of global CO₂ emissions. Yet it remains foundational to modern infrastructure, and cleaner alternatives have struggled to meet performance, scale, and cost demands.
companies.description: Material Evolution uses AI to engineer cement from industrial byproducts like steel slag, cutting emissions by over 80% compared to Portland cement. Their material performs better, cures faster, and fits seamlessly into existing supply chains, decarbonizing construction without compromise.

companies.name: Material Exchange
companies.one_liner: Digitizing textile sourcing so fabric can be sourced without leaving your seat.

companies.name: Matter
companies.one_liner: Self-cleaning filter that keeps microplastics out of rivers
companies.solution: If filters like this are built into washing machines and textile factories, a major source of microplastic pollution could be stopped at the source. It would protect rivers, soils and oceans without depending on people remembering to change a filter. Rivers, the soil beside them and the food grown in it would carry less of what our clothes shed, and a wash would stop being a way plastic reaches the sea.
companies.problem: Every time we wash synthetic clothes, tiny plastic fibres go down the drain and often end up in rivers and on farmland. Matter makes a filter for washing machines that traps those microplastics and cleans itself, so there are no cartridges to replace. Just empty the collected fibres every few weeks. Most machines carry no filter at all, so the fibres travel on to sewage works that were never built to catch anything so fine.

companies.name: Mazama
companies.one_liner: Volcano-grade heat, minus the volcano.
companies.solution: There's heat beneath every country on Earth. If it can be reached reliably, clean, round-the-clock power could be produced far beyond the volcanic regions that have always had it, giving many more nations a steady source of zero-carbon energy. Places with no hot spring and no obvious geology could still light and warm their homes from the ground beneath them, through the night and through the winter.
companies.problem: Geothermal energy usually only works in places with hot water close to the surface, like Iceland. Mazama drills into hot, dry rock and opens a network of cracks by circulating cold water through it, then uses that network to carry heat back up, reaching temperatures that deliver far more energy per well. Where geology already cooperates, a field means dozens of wells, each returning only a few megawatts of power.

companies.name: Metafuels
companies.one_liner: Brews clean jet fuel planes can already use
companies.solution: Methanol can be made from renewable electricity and captured carbon, which means the supply of clean jet fuel could be built rather than scavenged. That could finally give airlines a realistic way to cut emissions from flying at the scale the world needs. For anyone who flies to see family, and for the places that depend on being easy to reach, the journey would sit more lightly on the sky it crosses.
companies.problem: Airlines are being asked to use cleaner fuel, but there isn't nearly enough of it. Most of what exists is made from used cooking oil and animal fats, and there's only so much of that. Metafuels turns methanol into jet fuel that today's planes, engines and airports can take as a blend, with no changes to any of them.

companies.name: Metris Energy
companies.one_liner: Turns commercial buildings into solar-powered profit machines.

companies.name: MeVitae
companies.one_liner: Eliminates bias from your hiring process to build diverse, high-performing teams

companies.name: MiAlgae
companies.one_liner: Circular feed from distillery waste
companies.solution: If algae grown on waste can replace fish oil, the fishing pressure on wild stocks could ease, while the fish farming and pet food industries get a steady supply that doesn't depend on the ocean, or on a season that warm water can cut short. And distillery leftovers become something valuable. For the coastal places that live alongside those stocks, the small fish everything else in the sea feeds on get to stay where they are.
companies.problem: The omega-3 in fish feed and pet food comes mostly from wild fish caught in huge numbers for fish oil, rendered down rather than eaten by people. MiAlgae grows marine microalgae in the dark on the nutrient-rich liquid left over from whisky distilling, then harvests and dries it into a rich source of omega-3 without taking anything from the sea. The water that goes back to the distillery leaves cleaner than it arrived.

companies.name: microTERRA
companies.one_liner: What if, we could clean the water in fish farms by growing food in them?

companies.name: Microverse
companies.one_liner: What if, we teach coding to combat poverty?

companies.name: Mighty Buildings
companies.one_liner: Building environmentally friendly houses with a 3D-printer.

companies.name: MiiCare
companies.one_liner: Uses AI to keep our grandparents safe and supported while they age in place.

companies.name: Milvus Advanced
companies.one_liner: Powers green technologies without any rare metal.
companies.solution: Milvus Advance transforms cheap, common metals into high performing nanomaterials essential for green fuel/clean energy solutions.
companies.problem: Critical rare metals, like platinum and iridium, are essential for clean energy, but their costly and damaging extraction poses major supply chain risks.
companies.description: Milvus Advanced makes nano-materials from abundantly available metals like copper or nickel, enabling the clean energy transition without compromising on geopolitical risks, supply chain issues and extensive mining.

companies.name: Mirvie
companies.one_liner: Saving baby and mother's lives by predicting pregnancy complications with a single blood test months before they occur.

companies.name: Mission Barns
companies.one_liner: What if, we grow animal fat in labs to make better-tasting meat substitutes?

companies.name: Mission Zero
companies.one_liner: Pulls carbon out of the air, without heat.
companies.solution: If capturing carbon only needs a plug, it can happen almost anywhere with a grid connection or a solar farm, right next to the businesses that want to use or store the carbon. Carbon removal could shift from a few giant plants to equipment that can be ordered, shipped and installed like any other machine. A container standing beside an aggregate works or a fuel plant is a far easier thing to picture in an ordinary town than a power station.
companies.problem: Pulling carbon dioxide out of the air usually takes enormous amounts of heat, so capture plants end up wherever cheap heat is: next to geothermal wells or gas. Mission Zero captures carbon in a water-based liquid and releases it using electricity instead, in compact units that fit inside a shipping container. What comes out is pure carbon dioxide, the same thing industrial buyers now take by tanker from someone else's factory.

companies.name: Mitiga Solutions
companies.one_liner: AI and high-performance computing to predict, prevent and stop devastating wildfires.

companies.name: Mitti Labs
companies.one_liner: Pays rice farmers what satellites can prove.
companies.solution: Rice produces close to a tenth of human methane emissions. If satellites can verify reductions cheaply, millions of smallholder farmers could be paid for climate-friendly farming, cutting emissions while boosting their incomes. For a family growing rice on a single hectare, that is money arriving for something they can do with the fields they already have, in the season they already work, without leaving the village or changing the crop.
companies.problem: Flooded rice paddies release large amounts of methane, and draining fields at the right times can cut it. But proving it on millions of small farms is hard, since each family works about a hectare, too little for anyone to send an auditor to. Mitti Labs uses satellite radar to confirm when fields are drained, checks the results against gas measured in the fields themselves, and pays farmers for the methane they save.

companies.name: Modvion
companies.one_liner: Wooden towers that reach stronger wind.
companies.solution: Taller towers made from wood could reach stronger winds on inland sites, producing more clean energy while storing carbon in the tower itself. That could open up new places for wind power, far from the ports where the biggest turbines are built today. A field reached only by a country road could then hold a turbine as tall as the ones that arrive by sea, and the region around it gets more power from the same patch of ground.
companies.problem: Wind turbines produce more energy the higher they stand, but steel towers are limited in height because their sections must fit on roads. Modvion builds turbine towers from laminated Nordic spruce, pressed into curved modules that fit on a standard truck and are glued together on site. Developers who want to go higher today turn to concrete-and-steel hybrids, heavier and slower to raise, where a wooden tower stores carbon instead of carrying it.

companies.name: Molecular Attraction
companies.one_liner: What If, We Could Convince Mosquitoes To Stop Spreading Diseases?

companies.name: Molten Industries
companies.one_liner: Decarbonizes the world’s chemical and heavy industries.

companies.name: Mori
companies.one_liner: What if, we use silk proteins to stop food from going bad?

companies.name: MycoWorks
companies.one_liner: Making mushroom-based leather fashionable.

companies.name: Nala
companies.one_liner: Making remittances faster, cheaper, and borderless.
companies.solution: NALA is a Tanzanian fintech company providing affordable and reliable cross-border payment solutions for individuals and businesses, with a focus on Africa.
companies.problem: Developing economies like Asia and Africa rely on remittances for healthcare, education, and livelihoods. But traditional money transfer systems are slow, expensive, and riddled with hidden fees, costing families billions every year.
companies.description: NALA is a fintech platform that enables instant, low-cost money transfers to Africa and Asia using modern rails, local currency support, and no hidden fees. With banking features and offline accessibility, NALA turns remittances into a tool for financial empowerment.

companies.name: Nala Earth
companies.one_liner: Helps companies measure, improve, and report their impact on nature and biodiversity.
companies.solution: Nala enables businesses to understand their impacts and dependencies on the complex world of nature and biodiversity.
companies.problem: Neglecting nature as an optional concern comes at great financial and well-being costs for people and planet. While necessary, regulations can be hard to follow, and assessing a company’s potential negative impacts on e.g. land and water isn’t easy.
companies.description: Nala Earth simplifies the complex process of nature management, helping companies not only comply with leading regulations and frameworks but also identify risks and construct a comprehensive nature strategy.

companies.name: Nature's Fynd
companies.one_liner: What if, we make cream cheese and burgers from mushrooms?

companies.name: Nauto
companies.one_liner: What if, we used AI to make drivers drive more safely?

companies.name: Neoplants
companies.one_liner: Bioengineered superhero plants fighting air pollution.

companies.name: NetZeroNitrogen
companies.one_liner: Lets rice make its own fertiliser.
companies.solution: If the cheapest option for farmers is also the cleanest, change happens on its own, with no subsidy needed to make it worth doing. A natural fertiliser that costs less than urea could raise farm incomes, cut emissions and protect rivers across the world's rice-growing regions. For a family in the Mekong delta, the money that used to leave with every sack stays in the household at the end of the season.
companies.problem: Rice farmers spend a big share of their income on synthetic fertiliser, and much of it is lost into the air and water. NetZeroNitrogen offers a naturally occurring bacterium that farmers add to the water they already soak seeds in. It lives inside the plant and turns nitrogen from the air into food for the crop, so instead of buying a sack of urea and spreading it by hand several times a season, a farmer does one thing they were doing anyway.

companies.name: NEU Battery Materials
companies.one_liner: Battery waste becomes battery grade
companies.solution: As millions of LFP batteries reach the end of their lives, affordable recycling could turn a growing waste problem into a local source of lithium. It would make electric vehicles more circular and reduce the need for new mining. Lithium could go back into use near the places the old batteries were collected, rather than crossing the world to one of a handful of refineries and coming back as something new.
companies.problem: LFP batteries, now common in electric vehicles, are hard to recycle profitably because they contain no expensive metals like cobalt, so many end up stockpiled or burned. NEU Battery Materials uses a gentle electrochemical process to recover battery-grade lithium from them, using electricity and water. Crushed cells meet a liquid that lifts the lithium out at low voltage, with no furnace and no strong acid left to treat.

companies.name: Neurotrack
companies.one_liner: Early detection to put an end to Alzheimer's once and for all.

companies.name: Newcleo
companies.one_liner: Creates lead-cooled small modular reactors fueled by recycled nuclear waste.
companies.solution: Newcleo is a French nuclear technology company developing innovative lead-cooled fast reactors powered by recycled nuclear waste
companies.problem: Nuclear power generates long-lived radioactive waste that’s expensive and dangerous to store. At the same time, demand for clean baseload energy is growing, but new nuclear is costly and politically contentious.
companies.description: Newcleo designs next-generation lead-cooled fast reactors that can run on existing nuclear waste. Their closed-loop technology reduces radioactive stockpiles, slashes emissions, and delivers constant clean power, unlocking a circular future for nuclear energy.

companies.name: NFW
companies.one_liner: What if, we replace leather and plastics with plant-based alternatives?

companies.name: Nile
companies.one_liner: Farm to buyer, no middleman, just one click.
companies.solution: Developer of a food trading e-commerce platform designed to make nutritious food more accessible to consumers across the continent and beyond.
companies.problem: The traditional agricultural supply chain has many layers of intermediaries, which makes transactions opaque and leads to high costs and price uncertainty for both farmers and buyers. This fragmentation also contributes to food waste and makes it difficult for farmers to get fair prices.
companies.description: Nile's online marketplace directly connects farmers with commercial buyers, eliminating intermediaries. The platform digitizes the supply chain to provide transparent pricing, secure payments, and lower transaction costs for agricultural trading.

companies.name: Nilus
companies.one_liner: Distributing perfectly good, would-be-thrown-out, healthy food to low-income communities to end hunger.

companies.name: Nitricity
companies.one_liner: Turns air into fertilizer, with zero carbon footprint.

companies.name: Nitrovolt
companies.one_liner: Gives farmers the power to create their own green fertilizer right on-site

companies.name: Noon Energy
companies.one_liner: Stores renewable energy like a battery, using carbon and oxygen.
companies.solution: Noon Energy has developed a revolutionary battery technology for ultra-long duration energy storage of 100+ hours that stores energy using abundant materials, such as carbon and oxygen, instead of relatively scarce metals like lithium
companies.problem: Renewables are not always available due to factors like weather and seasonal changes, which makes it difficult to provide a consistent and reliable power supply. This creates a critical need for long-duration energy storage to ensure energy security. But current lithium-ion batteries are expensive and not well-suited for the task.
companies.description: Noon Energy builds long-duration batteries inspired by photosynthesis. Their system stores energy by splitting CO₂ into carbon and oxygen, delivering durable, scalable, and mineral-light energy storage to back up wind and solar 24/7.

companies.name: Northvolt
companies.one_liner: Making the world's greenest batteries.

companies.name: Nostics
companies.one_liner: Builds AI-powered diagnostic tools using nanotechnology for fast, portable disease detection.
companies.solution: Develops rapid, AI-powered diagnostic solutions using nanotechnology to enable fast, portable, and accurate disease detection
companies.problem: Getting diagnosis often depends on a centralized lab, which means that test results can take days to be delivered. This delay leads to frequent misdiagnosis and unnecessary treatments, which result in human suffering and wasted healthcare resources.
companies.description: Nostics creates portable, AI-powered diagnostic devices that identify bacterial infections in under five minutes—without lab equipment. Their nanotech and machine learning combo enables fast, accurate, point-of-care diagnostics that empower clinicians and slow antimicrobial resistance.

companies.name: Notpla
companies.one_liner: Developing plant-based plastic bags to end all plastic bags.

companies.name: Novoloop
companies.one_liner: Turns plastic waste into high-performance materials

companies.name: nsave
companies.one_liner: Provides trusted accounts to people from countries in unstable economies.
companies.solution: London based company providing people in financially unstable country (think high inflation, limited asset security, no investment opportunities) with global financial services and secure wealth management.
companies.problem: Millions living in high-inflation or politically unstable countries struggle to protect their savings. Local banks can be unreliable, and access to stable, secure global banking is often out of reach.
companies.description: nsave provides trusted, global accounts for people in vulnerable economies, that enables them to send, receive, and invest money in stable currencies, providing a safe alternative to unstable local banking.

companies.name: NuCicer
companies.one_liner: A chickpea that replaces processed protein.
companies.solution: If protein-rich chickpeas can be grown at scale, plant-based foods could become cheaper and simpler to make, starting in the field rather than the factory. That could help more people enjoy nutritious, sustainable protein. It would also mean the work of making protein begins in a growing season on a farm, rather than in a plant that first has to strip a cheaper seed back down to get there.
companies.problem: Most plant protein in food comes from peas or soy that are heavily processed to remove the starch, which takes energy and big factories. NuCicer breeds chickpeas with wild relatives gathered in south-east Turkey to produce seeds with about half as much protein again, reducing the need for that processing. A seed that reaches the mill already rich in protein means far less of what a maker buys is stripped away.

companies.name: Ocean Ecostructures
companies.one_liner: Turns ports and piers into thriving marine ecosystems.
companies.solution: They have developed their own "Life Boosting Units," a carbonated surface replicating marine natural substrate to regenerate biodiversity within three months. The startup has generated 3.7 tons of marine life, detected 300+ species, and captured 1.5 tons of CO2.
companies.problem: Traditional marine infrastructure like ports, seawalls, and breakwaters is made from lifeless concrete that harms biodiversity and disrupts natural habitats, worsening the ocean’s ecological decline.
companies.description: Ocean Ecostructures adds special surfaces to structures in the ocean to help bring marine life back. The company's tiles are designed to copy natural habitats, which attracts sea creatures and turns man-made coastlines into new ocean sanctuaries.

companies.name: Ocean Ledger
companies.one_liner: Geospatial intelligence that sees coastal risks coming.
companies.solution: The company specializes in providing high-resolution geospatial insights to assess and manage coastal ecosystems, focusing on areas such as shoreline movement, underwater topography, and ecosystem accounting
companies.problem: Organizations face risks like business interruptions, loan defaults, and large insurance losses due to coastal erosion and storm surges. Their ability to manage these risks is limited by outdated and inaccurate data.
companies.description: Ocean Ledger provides detailed and updated data on coastal physical risks like erosion and storm surges. Using information from satellites and advanced digital models to accurately track changes to coastlines, they help organizations, such as insurance companies and governments, to better understand and manage risks, and make more confident decisions about coastal properties and infrastructure.

companies.name: Ochre Bio
companies.one_liner: Letting livers live their best life, so you can do the same.

companies.name: Octarine Bio
companies.one_liner: Pigments without the poison
companies.solution: If natural pigments can match synthetic dyes on price and performance, fashion brands could clean up one of the dirtiest parts of making clothes without factories needing new machines. Rivers near dyeing hubs could run clean again. Colour has long been the part of a garment nobody could design away, and it becomes something a brand chooses as freely as the cloth, and something a town downstream of a dye house no longer has to live with.
companies.problem: Almost all the colour in our clothes comes from dyes made from petrochemicals, and dye waste often ends up in rivers. Octarine Bio uses microbes to grow natural pigments through fermentation, then uses enzymes to fine-tune the molecules so they dissolve and hold fast in existing dyeing machines, lasting through washing and sunlight. A mill can change what goes into the bath without changing the machines around it.

companies.name: Octavia Carbon
companies.one_liner: Pulling carbon straight out of Kenya’s skies.
companies.solution: Octavia Carbon is a Kenyan startup developing Direct Air Capture technology to remove CO₂ from the atmosphere and store it underground.
companies.problem: Meeting global climate targets requires more than just emissions reduction; we also need carbon removal. Global South has only minimally contributed to climate change, yet it is disproportionately affected.
companies.description: Octavia Carbon leverages Kenya's 93% renewable-powered grid and abundant basaltic rocks for geological storage, developing cost-effective, modular Direct Air Capture (DAC) systems. This technology extracts carbon directly from the air and stores it securely underground, providing a climate solution and a catalyst for green industrial growth in the region.

companies.name: Odys Aviation
companies.one_liner: Constructs hybrid-electric aircrafts that take off and land vertically, for regional travel.

companies.name: Oerth Bio
companies.one_liner: Giving plants the ultimate shield against disease and pests.

companies.name: Olio
companies.one_liner: What if, we build an app to ensure food is shared, not wasted?

companies.name: Oneka Technologies
companies.one_liner: Buoys that use wave motion to pump and desalinate seawater
companies.solution: Wave-powered desalination could bring clean water to coastal towns and islands without power plants or big infrastructure. As droughts become more common, it offers a simple, renewable way to turn the ocean into a source of drinking water. For a small island or a dry coastal town that has spent years waiting on a power line and a permit, water could instead start arriving each day from something moored quietly just offshore, where the waves already do the work.
companies.problem: Desalination plants need lots of power and produce concentrated brine that can harm marine life, putting them out of reach for many small coastal communities. Oneka's buoys use the motion of waves to pump seawater through filters and send fresh drinking water ashore, with no electricity needed to do it. There is no generator, no grid connection and nothing burning fuel, and what goes back to the sea is filtered before it leaves.

companies.name: Opna
companies.one_liner: Turns climate pledges into real-world action by financing planet-thriving projects.

companies.name: Orakl Oncology
companies.one_liner: Accelerates cancer drug development using patient tumor avatars.
companies.solution: Orakl Oncology develops AI-powered patient tumor avatars to enhance precision in oncology drug development.
companies.problem: The development of oncology drugs faces a 96% failure rate in clinical trials because traditional models fail to address the complexity and heterogeneity of cancer, leading to poor predictability and high costs.
companies.description: Orakl Oncology has developed an AI-powered techbio platform that creates individual "tumor avatars" by combining real-world patient data with advanced biology. This platform helps drug developers predict clinical outcomes and improve the success rate of trials.

companies.name: Orca Fraud
companies.one_liner: Takes down fraud with AI that spots the threats others miss, keeping businesses a step ahead.

companies.name: Ore Energy
companies.one_liner: Stores Tuesday's wind for Friday.
companies.solution: Europe already makes more clean electricity than it can use on its windiest days, and pays to throw the surplus away. Storage measured in days rather than hours turns that waste into the supply that covers the still week afterwards. The length of the longest windless stretch would stop deciding what a country keeps idling in reserve, and what households pay for plants that rarely run.
companies.problem: Solar and wind can fade for days at a time, and today gas plants stand by to fill the gap, held ready all year for a handful of still, cloudy spells. Ore Energy builds batteries that store electricity using iron, water and air, essentially rusting and un-rusting iron, which lets them hold power for days rather than hours. The containerised units breathe oxygen in to discharge and push it back out to charge.

companies.name: Oriole Networks
companies.one_liner: Builds ultra-efficient photonic networks, slashing AI’s energy hunger.
companies.solution: Oriole Networks has developed a novel way of using light to connect thousands of AI chips together. Once connected, the power of each graphics processing unit (GPU) is combined to form a “super-brain", which can be used to train advanced Large Language Models a hundred times faster, with a thousandth of the latency, while using a fraction of energy.
companies.problem: AI and data centers consume enormous amounts of energy, largely due to inefficient data movement. As demand for computing grows, so does the climate impact of digital infrastructure.
companies.description: Oriole Networks develops silicon photonics that move data using light instead of electricity. Their optical chips massively reduce energy use in data centers, enabling greener, faster, and more scalable AI and cloud computing.

companies.name: Osmoses
companies.one_liner: Separates industrial gases using membranes, not megawatts.
companies.solution: Osmoses is a U.S.-based company developing advanced membrane technology for efficient industrial gas separation.
companies.problem: Gas separation is a core step in many industries, from natural gas to hydrogen. But current systems rely on energy-hungry, emissions-heavy thermal processes like cryogenic distillation or pressure swing adsorption.
companies.description: Osmoses provides a patented membrane technology that acts as a filter to purify gas molecules with high flux and selectivity. This solution reduces industrial energy consumption by up to 90%

companies.name: Overstory
companies.one_liner: Flags the trees most likely to spark a wildfire
companies.solution: If utilities focus on the trees that matter most, the same budget could prevent more outages and fires, season after season. That means safer communities, more reliable power and smarter care for the trees that don't need cutting. For a town below a wooded ridge, it is the difference between a summer spent watching the hillside and wondering, and one spent getting on with everything else that summer is for.
companies.problem: Trees touching power lines cause many outages and some of the most destructive wildfires, but utilities usually trim on a fixed schedule rather than by risk. Overstory uses satellite and aerial imagery to measure individual trees along power lines and rank which ones pose the greatest danger. Height, species, growth rate and the gap to the wire are read from the images and joined to the utility's own maps, so crews go to the spans that need them most.
companies.description: Overstory's software uses AI and remote sensing data to create detailed vegetation maps. This allows utilities to create efficient and data-driven management plans, reducing vegetation-related risks and making operations more resilient.

companies.name: Overture Life
companies.one_liner: Saving couples money, time and emotional turmoil by developing IVF with better success rates.

companies.name: Oxyle
companies.one_liner: Destroys forever chemicals in water in minutes, not years.
companies.solution: Breakthrough PFAS catalytic destruction technology empowers industrial and environmental remediation companies in their fight against PFAS
companies.problem: PFAS, or "forever chemicals", contaminate drinking water globally leading to serious health outcomes. They’re nearly impossible to remove with traditional filtration systems, especially the short-chained PFAS.
companies.description: Oxyle has developed a treatment technology that uses nano-filtration and photochemical reduction to separate chains and eliminate even the toughest PFAS. It completely destroys the contaminants, leaving no residue, no toxic sludge, and delivering clean, safe water at scale.

companies.name: Oze
companies.one_liner: Supercharging SME growth in Africa and de-risking every loan.
companies.solution: Oze is a fintech company dedicated to transforming small business financing across Africa. By leveraging machine learning and advanced analytics, Oze connects financial institutions with SMEs through innovative digital lending solutions and business management tools.
companies.problem: Small businesses in Africa power local economies but lack tools to manage finances, access credit, or scale operations, keeping them in a cycle of stagnation and informality.
companies.description: Oze provides a business app with tools for bookkeeping, sales, and inventory management for SMEs. It also offers a lending management system for banks and microfinance banks that uses machine learning to assess creditworthiness, making small businesses better borrowers and reducing non-performing loans for lenders.

companies.name: Paebbl
companies.one_liner: Turns captured CO₂ into building material that's cleaner than concrete.
companies.solution: Paebbl is re-storing CO2 into raw materials. The proprietary technology mimics and speeds up Earth’s natural mineralization process by which our planet stores 3 gigatons of CO2 annually. As a result, they produce carbon-negative raw materials to be used across a variety of industries.
companies.problem: Cement and concrete are responsible for over 8% of global CO₂ emissions. Even with carbon capture, storing captured CO₂ safely and permanently remains a major challenge.
companies.description: Paebbl captures CO₂ and reacts it with industrial residues to create a strong, carbon-negative material. Their process permanently stores CO₂ and replaces traditional cement, building infrastructure while drawing down emissions.

companies.name: Pairwise
companies.one_liner: Saving harvests by giving produce super-immunity against diseases.

companies.name: Pear Bio
companies.one_liner: What if, we test cancer treatments on tumors grown on computer chips?

companies.name: Phaidra
companies.one_liner: Uses AI to make factories self-optimizing and ultra-efficient.
companies.solution: Provides artificial intelligence controls to optimize mission critical facilities with step function improvements in plant stability, energy efficiency and sustainability.
companies.problem: Industrial facilities like data centers, pharma plants, and manufacturing sites waste enormous energy due to outdated manual control systems. Traditional automation can't adapt in real-time to complex, changing conditions.
companies.description: Phaidra delivers an AI-powered control layer that continuously optimizes energy use and system performance in real time. Phaidra’s deep reinforcement learning AI makes industry smarter, greener, and more productive.

companies.name: Piclo
companies.one_liner: Making it easy to sell green energy at reasonable prices.

companies.name: PILI
companies.one_liner: Replaces toxic, non-recyclable ink with a greener, cleaner alternative.

companies.name: Pionix
companies.one_liner: Turns EV chargers into open-source intelligence hubs for the grid.
companies.solution: PIONIX is the globally leading open-source pioneer for EV charging technology. In 2020, PIONIX initiated EVerest, the first freely accessible and holistic software solution for the booming market of e-mobility.
companies.problem: As electric vehicles (EVs) flood the roads, the charging infrastructure risks becoming fragmented, closed, and proprietary. This limits innovation, slows adoption, and puts unnecessary strain on the energy grid. Without interoperability and smart integration, the EV revolution could stall before it truly takes off.
companies.description: Pionix provides software and engineering services built on the open-source EVerest software stack. This helps companies accelerate development, reduce integration risks, and get their EV charging products to market faster.

companies.name: Pivot Bio
companies.one_liner: Creating sustainable, zero-waste nitrogen fertilizers with the help of microbes.

companies.name: Plan A
companies.one_liner: Giving companies what they need to lower their carbon emissions.

companies.name: Planet A Foods
companies.one_liner: Crafts chocolatey bliss from plants, without a single cocoa bean in sight.

companies.name: Planetary
companies.one_liner: Grows protein that undercuts chicken.
companies.solution: If fermented protein can be made cheaply, right where sugar cane grows, it could become affordable enough to compete with chicken rather than sit above it as a premium. That could bring nutritious, sustainable protein to many more people around the world. It would arrive first in the countries that grow the cane, on the tables of people who were never going to pay extra for it, and who have the most to gain from a good meal costing less.
companies.problem: Fermented protein is a promising alternative to meat, but large fermentation tanks are scarce and costly. Planetary builds fermentation plants right next to sugar mills, using the mills' leftovers to grow a protein-rich fungus, and licenses the design to other sugar producers. The mill's cheap side streams and steam feed the tanks next door, so the protein is grown where the cane already grows rather than shipped to a plant far away.

companies.name: Planted
companies.one_liner: Solar farms that follow the hillside.
companies.solution: If solar can be built on slopes and awkward plots, far more land becomes usable and less farmland is lost. Projects could use less steel, move faster and win more local support, helping clean power grow in places that were written off before. For a county weighing up a hillside nobody farms, or a ravine on the edge of town, that turns land written off as unbuildable into somewhere the lights can come from.
companies.problem: Most solar farms need flat land, so developers flatten hills and fields before building, which is slow, expensive and unpopular with neighbours. Planted designs each solar layout to follow the natural shape of the land, and uses robots to install the foundations without grading the site first. Dense rows run across slopes and irregular parcels, and the machines drive each post to the depth that piece of ground calls for.

companies.name: Polaron
companies.one_liner: Uses AI to accelerate advanced materials development from years down to days.
companies.solution: Polaron’s generative AI platform uses microstructural image data to learn the direct mapping between process, structure, and performance, enabling manufacturers to explore thousands of material designs in under a day, models that would take physics‑based simulations decades boosting battery energy density by ~10% and cutting R&D time from hundreds of weeks to mere hours. It trains bespoke models on small datasets privately on customer hardware, making it efficient, scalable, and IP‑safe.
companies.problem: Traditional methods for developing advanced materials are slow, costly, and inefficient, which can take years due to complex manufacturing processes.
companies.description: Polaron uses AI to accelerate the materials development timeline from years to days. Their technology reduces prototyping, provides deeper insights, and optimizes both material performance and manufacturing costs.

companies.name: Praxis Labs
companies.one_liner: Using VR to help companies rethink biases and become more inclusive.

companies.name: Predium
companies.one_liner: Maps a building's path to zero carbon
companies.solution: If this works at scale, housing associations and cities could plan upgrades for thousands of buildings in the time it now takes to survey one. That could speed up the renovation of older, poorly documented buildings that are too often left until last. For the people living in them, it means a warmer flat and a smaller bill arriving years sooner than a place on the waiting list would ever have allowed.
companies.problem: Many landlords don't know how much carbon their buildings emit, and finding out usually means paying a consultant to visit each property and come back months later. Predium builds an energy and carbon model of a building from just its address, then ranks which upgrades would cut the most emissions for the money. Satellite imagery and public records fill in what the address alone cannot say, without anyone setting foot on site.
companies.description: Predium offers a digital platform that makes it radically simple for real estate players to measure, manage, and Predium's platform uses AI and satellite imagery to complete building data and link it to financial and sustainability metrics. This enables users to simulate investment scenarios and prioritize based on data rather than working in silos.

companies.name: Prellis Biologics
companies.one_liner: Saving lives by 3D printing human tissue and organs.

companies.name: PreWave
companies.one_liner: Uses AI to predicts and expose supply chain risks.
companies.solution: specializing in supply chain risk intelligence, utilizing artificial intelligence (AI) to monitor and analyze supplier data
companies.problem: Supply chains are increasingly fragile and complex, with companies lacking visibility into risks beyond their immediate suppliers. This leads to costly disruptions, brand damage, and difficulty complying with new regulations.
companies.description: Prewave’s AI-powered platform scans millions of online sources in 50+ languages to spot supply chain risks before they escalate, from factory fires to human rights violations. It turns overwhelming amounts of global data into actionable intelligence, allowing companies to act fast, stay compliant, and build responsible, resilient supply chains. It’s like an early warning system for the entire world economy.

companies.name: Project Eaden
companies.one_liner: Spins plant-based meat like textile fibers.
companies.solution: Proprietary wet protein fiber spinning technology adapted from the textile industry to produce ultra-realistic plant-based meats with the look, taste, and chew of animal meat
companies.problem: Most plant-based meats fall short on texture and flavor, keeping meat lovers unconvinced and slowing the shift away from environmentally harmful livestock farming.
companies.description: Project Eaden uses advanced fiber-spinning tech from the textile industry to create ultra-realistic plant-based meats. Their unique approach replicates the muscle structure of real meat, delivering taste, texture, and sizzle that even carnivores crave.

companies.name: Proxima Fusion
companies.one_liner: Building a star for the power grid.
companies.solution: Fusion could provide steady, clean power without depending on rivers, coastlines or special geology. If it works commercially, clean electricity could be produced almost anywhere, starting with old power plant sites that already have grid connections in place. For places with no river to dam, no coastline and no hot rock beneath them, steady power would come down to a decision someone makes rather than a map they were handed.
companies.problem: Grids need clean power that's there whenever it's needed, not just when the sun shines or the wind blows. Today that gap is mostly filled by gas and coal. Proxima Fusion is designing stellarators, fusion machines that hold superheated plasma in place using twisted superconducting magnets, a shape that lets the plasma burn continuously rather than in pulses. The shape of those magnets and the engineering of the plant around them are worked out together, in one simulation loop.
companies.description: Proxima Fusion is building the first generation of fusion power plants using quasi-isodynamic (QI) stellarators. The clearest, most robust path to putting fusion on the grid.

companies.name: Proximie
companies.one_liner: Creating world-class robot-surgeons.

companies.name: PULSETRAIN
companies.one_liner: Keeps an electric car battery going even when one cell fails
companies.solution: Batteries that last longer mean fewer new ones, and less lithium and nickel mined for every car on the road. Used and mismatched cells could get a second life, and a car's performance could improve through software updates instead of new hardware. For a driver, that means a car that gets better over the years it is owned, and a battery that carries on long after one weak cell would once have ended it.
companies.problem: An electric car battery is only as good as its weakest cell, and when a few cells fade the whole pack is often retired. PULSETRAIN builds the power electronics into the battery itself and controls every cell individually, so the pack keeps working even when some cells weaken or fail. The inverter, charger and management all sit inside the pack, which sends alternating current straight to the motor.

companies.name: Puna Bio
companies.one_liner: Supercharges crops with biological innovations that boost yields, cut carbon, and revive soil.

companies.name: Qarbotech
companies.one_liner: Supercharging plants with a biocompatible boost for faster, greener growth.

companies.name: Qida
companies.one_liner: Turns your home into the best hospital you'll never check into.
companies.solution: Barcelona-based company that operates in the health and social care space by providing solutions to transform home-care and healthcare at scale.
companies.problem: Hospitals are overcrowded, costly, and emotionally draining. Especially for patients with chronic illnesses, aging populations, or those in recovery. Our traditional healthcare system(s) wasn’t designed for personalized, ongoing care at scale. Meanwhile, millions suffer from fragmented, impersonal, or insufficient support once they leave the hospital.
companies.description: Qida brings healthcare home, literally. They combine trained caregivers, doctors, nurses, and therapists into one coordinated system. Each patient gets a personalized care plan managed by a dedicated coordinator, supported by digital tools that keep everyone connected. This radical reimagining of care, (patient-first, home-based, and designed for dignity) improves quality of life for patients, eases the burden on families, and lowers costs for public health systems, all while raising the standard and value of the caregiving profession.

companies.name: Quaise Energy
companies.one_liner: What if, we could get limitless, clean and free energy by digging really, really deep holes?

companies.name: Queens Carbon
companies.one_liner: Cement without the carbon hangover
companies.solution: Queens Carbon produces carbon-neutral cement additives that cut industrial CO₂ emissions at scale. Their technology works inside existing plants, giving producers a simple path to cleaner cement.
companies.problem: Cement is everywhere. In our roads, bridges, and buildings, but making it is one of the dirtiest industrial processes on Earth, responsible for nearly 8% of global CO₂ emissions. Traditional fixes require tearing down and rebuilding plants with costly new equipment, which most producers simply cannot afford.
companies.description: Queens Carbon has invented a way to make cement that slashes emissions without replacing furnaces. Their drop-in ingredient, Q-SCM, uses lower heat, captures carbon in the process, and can replace up to half of traditional cement in concrete mixes. It’s plug-and-play climate tech at industrial scale.

companies.name: R3 Robotics
companies.one_liner: Robots turn junked EV systems into material mines
companies.solution: As millions of electric vehicles reach the end of their lives, robots could turn them into a steady source of sorted copper, aluminium and battery materials. Some batteries could also get a second life, making the shift to electric transport more circular. The metal already above ground in yesterday's cars would find its way into tomorrow's, instead of being dug out of a hillside somewhere far away all over again.
companies.problem: Old electric vehicle batteries are mostly taken apart by hand, a slow and risky job at high voltage, or simply shredded, which mixes valuable materials together. R3 Robotics uses robots with machine vision that adapt to each battery design, dismantling packs and motors cleanly and safely. The robot maps the fasteners and seams of each pack and plans its own path, so the materials come out sorted rather than mixed.

companies.name: Reality Defender
companies.one_liner: Stopping deepfakes before they fool anyone.

companies.name: RecupeRe Metals
companies.one_liner: Copper wire without the mining
companies.solution: Electric cars, wind turbines and power grids all need copper. If recycled copper can go straight back into electrical use, Europe could rely less on mining and foreign refineries, keeping this valuable metal circulating closer to home. Copper that once dropped out of electrical duty into pipes and castings would keep doing the work it was made for, staying in the wires and coils of the places where it was first put to use.
companies.problem: The copper wire inside motors and generators must be extremely pure, so scrap copper usually goes back through energy-hungry refineries, mostly outside Europe, or gets downgraded into plumbing. RecupeRe Metals has developed a process that turns recycled copper directly into high-quality electrical wire. The grain structure is shaped through the mechanical processing itself, so the wire never goes back to the furnace.

companies.name: Recycleye
companies.one_liner: Reinventing the economics of recycling

companies.name: RedoxBlox
companies.one_liner: Turns industrial heat into a clean battery.
companies.solution: RedoxBlox delivers clean, long-duration energy storage for heavy industry. Their system gives factories fossil-free heat on demand. Scalable, affordable, and designed for the toughest industrial processes.
companies.problem: Steel, cement, and chemical plants run on furnaces that need steady, extreme heat. Today that heat comes mostly from coal and gas, and clean energy solutions don’t address high-temperature heat storage at industrial scale, making industrial heat one of the single hardest sources of carbon emissions to cut.
companies.description: RedoxBlox has built a thermal battery that stores renewable electricity as heat. When needed, the system releases that energy as either very high-temperature heat (up to 1,500 °C) or electricity. Because it’s modular and retrofittable, it can slot into existing plants without replacing furnaces or building new infrastructure.This means heavy industry can finally ditch fossil fuels without compromising performance in a scalable, flexible, and totally new way.

companies.name: Redwood Materials
companies.one_liner: What if, we could recycle old electric cars into new electric cars?

companies.name: ReGrow Ag
companies.one_liner: Using satellite data to get the agricultural industry to reduce emissions.

companies.name: Relation Therapeutics
companies.one_liner: Merges machine learning and human genetics into life-saving therapies.

companies.name: Relyion Energy
companies.one_liner: Unlocks renewables for industries, grids, and communities everywhere.
companies.solution: Relyion Energy Inc. specializes in refurbishing and integrating second-life EV batteries into AI-optimized stationary energy storage systems
companies.problem: As the world transitions to renewable energy, storing that energy safely and affordably becomes a major bottleneck. Lithium-ion batteries dominate the market but are expensive, flammable, and not ideal for long-duration or grid-scale storage—limiting progress on decarbonizing electricity.
companies.description: Relyion Energy has created a next-generation zinc-based battery that’s low-cost, non-flammable, and scalable for grid storage. Unlike lithium-ion, their chemistry is inherently safe and made from abundant materials—reducing cost by 60% and eliminating fire risk. This breakthrough opens the door to reliable, affordable renewable energy around the clock.

companies.name: Renasens
companies.one_liner: Blended textiles close the loop
companies.solution: If mixed, dyed clothes can be turned back into new textiles, the mountains of used clothing collected across Europe become a resource instead of waste. Fashion could finally start to close the loop. The bales piling up behind collection points across the continent would become something a spinner buys rather than something a town pays to burn, and the shirt someone wore out could come back as the one they buy next.
companies.problem: Less than one per cent of old clothes are recycled into new ones, because most garments are blends of fibres like cotton and polyester, and dyed. Renasens uses carbon dioxide under pressure, without water, to remove dyes and separate blended fabrics back into clean fibres ready to be spun again. Under pressure it moves through fabric like a gas and dissolves like a solvent, so the fibres come out whole rather than broken down.

companies.name: Resortecs
companies.one_liner: Melts seams to unleash garment recycling at scale

companies.name: Retein
companies.one_liner: What if, we mimic the behavior of plankton to purify water cheaply and at scale?

companies.name: Reverion
companies.one_liner: A power plant that keeps its carbon.
companies.solution: Small farms could become mini power plants that both supply flexible, clean electricity and remove carbon for good. Getting more out of the same biogas means the countryside could play a much bigger role in the energy transition. A village with a herd and a digester would have something to give the grid on a still winter evening, when the wind has dropped, and a way to put its own carbon safely out of circulation for good.
companies.problem: Farm biogas plants usually burn their gas in engines that waste more than half the energy as heat. Reverion's system converts biogas into electricity without burning it, which is far more efficient, and separates out the carbon dioxide in a pure stream ready to be stored. Run in reverse, it can store surplus power as fuel. The gas is converted in a stack of ceramic cells rather than in a piston, so the same digester yields more.

companies.name: RIFT
companies.one_liner: Clean, circular industrial heating from iron powder
companies.solution: Iron powder can be shipped and stored like coal, but without the emissions, so hydrogen can be made where power costs least and used where the metal is regenerated. If this works at scale, factories could switch fuel without waiting on a pipeline or a grid upgrade, bringing clean heat to places those networks can't easily reach. For the towns built around those plants, the work stays and the smoke goes.
companies.problem: Factories that need high-temperature steam around the clock usually burn gas or coal, and often can't switch to electricity or hydrogen because the site sits far from any pipeline and holds no spare grid capacity. RIFT supplies boilers that burn fine iron powder, releasing heat as the metal oxidises. The leftover rust is collected and turned back into iron using low-carbon hydrogen, so the same metal can be used again and again.

companies.name: Rize
companies.one_liner: Rice that feeds families and cools the planet.
companies.solution: Rize makes rice farming profitable and sustainable by turning greener practices into verified carbon credits. Farmers get better income and the world gets lower emissions.
companies.problem: Rice is a staple food for half the world but growing it releases huge amounts of methane, a greenhouse gas many times stronger than CO₂. Farmers in Asia and other regions often earn very little and have no financial reason to change how they grow it. The global push for regenerative agriculture has a missing link: economic viability for the people actually doing the farming.
companies.description: Rize helps farmers adopt climate-smart rice practices that cut methane and use less water. They provide training and tools, track the impact, and connect farmers to global carbon markets. This way farmers earn more while farming in a way that helps the planet.

companies.name: Roam
companies.one_liner: Accelerates clean mobility in emerging markets with electric motorcycles and buses.

companies.name: Robeauté
companies.one_liner: Sends microrobots to brain tumors surgery can't reach
companies.solution: Today, what a surgeon can treat depends on whether a safe straight path to it exists. A robot that can move through the brain in three dimensions could change that, making parts of the brain reachable that are currently written off. Neurological disease is among the hardest medicine to follow, because getting to the tissue is itself the risk. If that stops being true, diagnosing a brain disease, watching how it changes and treating it could become one process rather than three separate dangers.
companies.problem: Some brain tumours sit where rigid, straight surgical tools cannot safely reach, tucked behind a vessel or beneath the areas that govern movement and speech, and so they are treated cautiously or not at all. Robeauté is developing a microrobot no larger than a grain of rice that moves through brain tissue in three dimensions rather than along a straight line. It is designed to take targeted biopsies, deliver therapies to a precise point and collect data from the individual patient, with less disturbance to the brain than a rigid instrument causes.
companies.description: Robeauté has created microrobots no bigger than a grain of rice. These tiny, AI‑guided robots can enter the brain through a small opening. They move through curved pathways to reach hard‑to‑access areas, where they can collect samples, deliver treatments, or gather data. Doing more with far less disruption and ushering in a new era of precision medicine.

companies.name: Rology
companies.one_liner: Uses AI and remote technology to provide accurate medical scans, improving healthcare in difficult-to-reach areas.

companies.name: Rondo Energy
companies.one_liner: Powers industries with heat batteries that cut costs and wipe out emissions using renewable energy.

companies.name: Root
companies.one_liner: Cuts the climate cost of every cow.
companies.solution: If cutting methane becomes cheap enough, it could become standard on farms everywhere rather than something only premium supply chains pay for. That could bring down emissions from the world's cattle herd, one of the biggest sources of methane. Most cattle are given nothing at all today, and a dose a farmer can afford unprompted is what changes that, herd by herd, in the countries where the herd is still growing.
companies.problem: Feed additives that cut methane from cows already exist, but they cost more per animal than most farmers are willing to pay, so they spread only where a dairy, a retailer or a carbon scheme picks up the bill. Root is developing a new molecule that blocks the reaction in a cow's stomach that turns feed into methane, designed to be effective at a much lower cost per animal. It goes in as a small daily dose, mixed into the feed a herd already eats.

companies.name: Rootglobal
companies.one_liner: Turns climate action and farm data into profitable opportunities.
