companies.solution: Root Global offers a platform for food and beverage companies to manage and reduce supply chain GHG emissions.​
companies.problem: Companies are under pressure to disclose and mitigate climate risk, but most lack the tools to translate emissions data into business strategy, or understand the financial impacts of inaction. Most only know product-level averages, not what happens in the fields, making climate risk invisible and action slow.
companies.description: Root Global is a climate strategy platform that equips business leaders with actionable insights connecting carbon data, regulations, and financial risk in one dashboard. It transforms sustainability from a reporting burden and missed opportunity into a competitive advantage.

companies.name: Rubi Labs
companies.one_liner: Turns air pollution into fashion’s future
companies.solution: Rubi Labs transforms CO₂ emissions into high‑quality, biodegradable textile fibers made of pure cellulose. Their enzyme-powered system plugs into today’s clothing factories, creating carbon-negative materials at scale.
companies.problem: The fashion industry generates a huge amount of carbon emissions, especially from fabric production using virgin cotton or polyester. These fabrics harm forests, use lots of water and land, and still pollute when disposed.
companies.description: Rubi Labs captures carbon emissions (often waste gas) from factories and uses enzymes (mimicing nature) to turn that CO₂ into cellulose. That cellulose can be spun into yarn and fabric without needing trees, water, or land. Their process is carbon-negative, water-neutral, and fits into existing textile production, enabling climate-positive fashion at industrial scale.

companies.name: Running Tide
companies.one_liner: What if, we could slow down climate change by putting seaweed on the ocean floor?

companies.name: RxAll
companies.one_liner: Bringing safe, high-quality medicines to the African continent with tech that verifies and tracks every pill in real time.

companies.name: Sabi
companies.one_liner: Turning Africa’s smallest shops into the biggest force for sustainable growth
companies.solution: Sabi is a Nigerian-based B2B platform that digitizes informal trade networks, offering SMEs streamlined sourcing, distribution, and financial services, with a growing focus on ethical commodities through its TRACE program.
companies.problem: Climate change is driving more frequent and severe wildfires, threatening ecosystems, property, and lives. Yet most forests lack real-time monitoring, making prevention reactive and often too late.
companies.description: Sabi creates solar-powered sensors that “listen” to forests, capturing environmental sounds and data. With AI, they detect early fire risks and illegal activities that enables local communities and authorities to act before disaster strikes.

companies.name: Sava
companies.one_liner: Monitors blood sugar through a tiny skin patch
companies.solution: If continuous monitoring becomes affordable, millions more people could manage diabetes with confidence, including in places where no monitor reaches the market today. In the future, the same patch could track other health signals too, among them lactate, ketones and cortisol, making personalised health insights part of everyday life. That is a quieter kind of care: fewer fingersticks, fewer surprises, more ordinary days.
companies.problem: Most people with diabetes still prick their fingers several times a day because continuous glucose monitors are expensive and often not covered by insurance. Sava is developing a small, affordable skin patch that sits shallower under the skin than today's monitors, tracks blood sugar continuously and sends the readings to a phone. Instead of one moment in the day, the person sees the whole trend and can act on it.

companies.name: Sava Health
companies.one_liner: THE MOST POWERFUL BIOSENSOR EVER CREATED
companies.solution: Sava’s novel wearable microsensor uses ultra‑small, shallow microneedles just beneath the skin to provide accurate, pain‑free, cost‑effective continuous glucose monitoring validated in clinical trials for up to 10 days, unmatched by any other platform.
companies.problem: People with diabetes need to track glucose all the time, but today's devices can be painful, costly, and hard to use. That puts continuous monitoring out of reach for most, even though regular tracking is crucial for health.
companies.description: Sava has invented a wearable microsensor that uses tiny, pain-free needles to track glucose in real time just under the skin. It lasts up to ten days and sends data directly to a smartphone. Accurate, affordable, and much gentler than current systems.

companies.name: Savor
companies.one_liner: Cooks butter out of carbon and hydrogen.
companies.solution: If fat can be made in a factory at a competitive price, food and cosmetics companies could stop relying on crops linked to deforestation, buying instead from a plant sited wherever hydrogen is cheap. That could ease pressure on tropical forests while keeping the foods people love on the table. For the forests themselves, and for everything living in them, it is a hectare of ground that never has to be cleared at all.
companies.problem: Fats like butter and palm oil come from animals or plantations, and palm oil expansion has driven large-scale deforestation across South East Asia. Savor makes fat without farms, combining carbon and hydrogen over a catalyst into the same fat molecules found in butter and plant oils. Bonded to glycerol, the result behaves like the fat it replaces, melting the way a biscuit or a face cream needs it to.
companies.description: Savor uses thermochemical processes to create real fats by following nature’s own blueprints. Their platform produces versatile, functional fats and oils directly from carbon sources without conventional animal or plant agriculture.

companies.name: Scipher Medicine
companies.one_liner: A science-based psychic to predict your body's reaction to medicine.

companies.name: Seabound
companies.one_liner: The fleet that plunders pollution at sea.
companies.solution: Develops onboard retrofit carbon capture technology for ships, capturing up to 95% of CO₂ emissions directly from exhaust gases.
companies.problem: Global shipping emits more than a billion tons of CO₂ every year. Most ships still run on heavy fuel oil, and replacing fleets with green vessels is too slow and expensive. The sector urgently needs ways to cut emissions now.
companies.description: Seabound builds carbon capture systems that install directly onto existing cargo ships. Their compact devices trap up to 95 percent of CO₂ from smokestacks and turn it into solid minerals that can be safely stored or reused. This low-cost, install-anywhere solution cuts emissions today without waiting for new green ships.

companies.name: SeaPattern
companies.one_liner: Turning overlooked currents into clean electricity.
companies.solution: SeaPattern delivers systems that boost renewable energy from existing hydropower plants. Their technology makes power generation more efficient without building new dams or disrupting ecosystems.
companies.problem: Oceans hold massive energy, but we only tap a tiny share of it. Most hydropower plants miss the currents left after turbines, wasting clean energy that could power homes and industries.
companies.description: SeaPattern installs hydrokinetic turbines in the water channels downstream of existing hydropower stations. Their AI maps water flow, helping place turbines where currents still have power. This approach can increase electricity output by up to 10 percent using the infrastructure already in place.

companies.name: Sensegrass
companies.one_liner: Makes farming smarter by boosting crop yields and cutting chemical use with agrotech and AI.

companies.name: SepPure
companies.one_liner: Filters chemicals with nanotech that’s 580x (that's a lot) more energy-efficient than traditional methods.

companies.name: Shara
companies.one_liner: Unlocks financial access in Africa with tech that empowers communities to save, borrow, and grow.

companies.name: Shellworks
companies.one_liner: Plastic that grows and dies
companies.solution: If compostable packaging can match plastic on cost and performance, brands could switch without compromise, choosing a jar that survives a year on a shelf and still belongs in the garden heap. That could mean far less plastic waste piling up in landfills and nature. For anyone who has ever wondered where an empty jar ends up, the answer would finally be a simple one, and it would end in ordinary garden soil.
companies.problem: Most cosmetic jars and packaging are made from conventional plastic, and most 'compostable' alternatives only break down in industrial facilities that households cannot reach. Shellworks makes packaging from a material produced by bacteria fed on waste like used cooking oil, which store it inside their cells as an energy reserve. Compounded into pellets, it works on standard factory equipment and can break down in a home compost.

companies.name: Shelly XU Design
companies.one_liner: Zero-waste fashion with no fabric scraps.
companies.solution: SXD uses patent-published AI to eliminate material waste, generating zero waste products that enable ~80% reduction in CO2 and significant cost savings.
companies.problem: The fashion industry creates over 90 million tons of textile waste each year. Much of this waste comes before clothes are even made, from inefficient cutting patterns that leave large scraps on the factory floor.
companies.description: Shelly Xu Design (SXD) uses AI-powered pattern making that arranges garment pieces like puzzle pieces. This method leaves no fabric waste, reduces carbon emissions, and still produces beautiful, high-quality clothing.

companies.name: Shipzero
companies.one_liner: Helps global freight transport get to net-zero with software that turns emissions data into smart, green decisions.

companies.name: Smartex
companies.one_liner: Using AI to spot fabric flaws, cut waste, and collect primary production data - fashion just got smarter.

companies.name: Solstice
companies.one_liner: What if, we leverage community buying power to give everyone access to solar?

companies.name: Solugen
companies.one_liner: What if, we make the chemicals we need from sugar, not petroleum?

companies.name: Sound Agriculture
companies.one_liner: What if, we convince microbes to help us grow better plants?

companies.name: Source.ag
companies.one_liner: Forecasts greenhouse harvest weeks ahead.
companies.solution: If one expert can manage many more greenhouses with AI support, high-tech growing could spread far beyond the few countries that lead it today, where the best yields have clustered for a generation. More regions could grow fresh vegetables locally, efficiently and all year round. That means a tomato picked a short drive from the table, in places where winter has always meant shipping it halfway around the world.
companies.problem: Greenhouse growers still rely heavily on experts walking the crop and counting fruit by eye to plan harvests, and those experts are increasingly hard to find. Source.ag uses AI to combine greenhouse sensors, plant measurements and weather forecasts to predict harvests weeks ahead and manage watering. It works alongside the climate computer a site already runs, so a grower keeps the glasshouse and gains the forecast.

companies.name: Sourceful
companies.one_liner: Revolutionizing packaging, by making it frictionless for companies to go green and cut waste from their supply chains.

companies.name: Space Forge
companies.one_liner: Manufactures chips in orbit, ships them home
companies.solution: Crystals grown in space could lead to more efficient electronics for everything from power grids to communications, losing less energy every time current passes through them. If returning materials from orbit becomes routine, manufacturing in space could move from science fiction to industry. Orbit would slowly become somewhere we make the things we use down here, rather than only somewhere we look back down from.
companies.problem: The materials used in advanced chips work best when their crystals are nearly flawless, but gravity makes that hard to achieve on Earth, because convection and contact with the crucible leave defects behind. Space Forge sends a small satellite with a furnace into orbit to grow semiconductor crystals in the vacuum and weightlessness of space, then aims to bring them back to Earth under an unfolding, reusable heat shield.

companies.name: Sparxell
companies.one_liner: Color you can compost.
companies.solution: Sparxell is the creator of the world’s first 100 per cent plant-based biodegradable colour pigments, glitters, sequins, and films
companies.problem: Most colors today come from toxic chemical dyes, mined minerals, or plastics like glitter. These contribute to pollution, microplastics, and toxic waste throughout their lifecycle.
companies.description: Sparxell uses plant-based cellulose to craft colors, glitters, sequins, and films inspired by structures found in butterfly wings and peacock feathers. This process creates vibrant, fade-resistant hues without dyes, microplastics, or toxins.

companies.name: Spoor
companies.one_liner: Deep-tech saving birds from flying into wind turbines to combat climate change.

companies.name: SQUAKE
companies.one_liner: Giving the transportation industry no reason to not calculate and compensate for their emissions.

companies.name: Stegra
companies.one_liner: What if, we could make steel using electricity and water?

companies.name: Still Bright
companies.one_liner: Refines copper without the furnace.
companies.solution: If copper can be refined cleanly right at the mine, deposits and old mine waste that were once written off could become valuable. That could help supply the copper the energy transition needs, with far fewer emissions. Refining would follow the ore rather than the trade routes, and the copper wiring inside a new home, a new car or a new stretch of grid could begin a great deal closer to where it finally ends up.
companies.problem: Much of the world's copper has to be shipped to distant smelters that heat ore to extreme temperatures, and some ore is too impure or too dilute to process at all. Still Bright uses an electrochemical process that pulls copper out of ore at near room temperature, using electricity instead of furnaces. A vanadium liquid strips the copper and then cycles back through the cell for reuse, and the sulphur leaves as a separate stream.

companies.name: Stitch
companies.one_liner: The API layer that ties Africa’s money systems together.
companies.solution: Stitch offers developers and enterprises reliable infrastructure to build and scale financial services in African markets. Their tools simplify payments, data access, and identity so businesses can launch products faster.
companies.problem: Africa’s financial systems are notoriously fragmented. Payments move slowly across banks, wallets, and markets. This makes building reliable financial products expensive and slow, holding back fintech innovation and financial inclusion.
companies.description: Stitch provides API infrastructure that makes it easy to build and scale financial services in Afric, from payments to banking to identity. With Stitch, companies can launch products faster, move money more efficiently, and create radically better financial experiences for consumers and businesses alike.

companies.name: Strong by Form
companies.one_liner: Concrete strength without the carbon
companies.solution: Cement and steel together cause a large share of global emissions. If shaped timber can take on jobs only concrete can do today, architects could design ambitious buildings from wood, with the long spans and curves that used to mean pouring on site, and the same approach could make lighter parts for trains and vehicles. Buildings would come from forests rather than quarries, and would feel it from the inside.
companies.problem: Timber is a low-carbon building material, but it mostly comes as flat panels and straight beams, sized by the weakest direction of a uniform board, so long spans and curved structures still rely on concrete and steel. Strong by Form lays wood fibres along the exact paths that loads travel, and shapes them with robots into strong, curved timber elements. Fibre sits only where the load runs, so little is spent holding up the part itself.

companies.name: Submer
companies.one_liner: Cooling down computers with less than half of the current required energy.

companies.name: SunFi
companies.one_liner: Making solar power affordable and accessible for everyone in Africa.

companies.name: Sway
companies.one_liner: Seaweed replacing plastic bags
companies.solution: If seaweed can replace plastic film on existing production lines, packaging could change one supplier at a time, without waiting for factories to be rebuilt. Seaweed farming could grow too, a crop that needs no fresh water, fertiliser or land. That is a harvest that adds nothing to the pressure on farmland or fresh water, and a mailer that can finish its life quietly in a compost heap rather than in a hedgerow.
companies.problem: Plastic film for bags and packaging is cheap, fast to make and almost never recycled, partly because thin film wraps around the screens at sorting plants. Sway makes a seaweed-based material, compounded into pellets, that runs on the same equipment used to make plastic bags today, so manufacturers can switch without new investment. A converter keeps its blown-film lines and changes only what goes into them.

companies.name: Sweep
companies.one_liner: Sweeps carbon and ESG data into one platform - track, disclose, and act with style.

companies.name: Sycai Medical
companies.one_liner: Detects silent cancers before they can hide from doctors.
companies.solution: Sycai Medical provides AI tools that act as a second set of eyes for radiologists, flagging hidden cancers in routine imaging before they progress. Their technology is designed to improve early detection and patient outcomes worldwide.
companies.problem: Pancreatic and liver cancers are often diagnosed too late, when treatment options are limited. Radiologists must review thousands of images, and small lesions are easy to miss. This delay costs patients the chance of early, life-saving intervention.
companies.description: Sycai Medical develops AI-powered software that works with CT and MRI scans. It detects and classifies abdominal lesions and predicts which ones are likely to develop into cancer. By integrating directly into hospital systems, it helps radiologists catch cancers earlier, more accurately, and at scale.

companies.name: Syre
companies.one_liner: Textile waste becomes fashion's raw material
companies.solution: If old clothes can become new ones at scale, fashion could stop depending on oil for polyester, one of its most-used materials, and stop leaning on the bottle stream to get there. Worn-out garments would become a valuable resource instead of a growing mountain of waste. The jacket at the back of a wardrobe would be the beginning of the next one, wherever in the world it was worn out, and the mills making it would draw on what people already own.
companies.problem: Most 'recycled' polyester clothing is actually made from drinks bottles, pulled out of a working bottle loop, while old clothes are burned, dumped or shipped abroad in bales. Syre breaks down used polyester textiles into their basic building blocks and rebuilds them into new polyester that's as good as virgin material. Shredded garments have their metal and hard points taken out, and what comes back is a chip a spinner can run exactly as it runs material made from oil.
companies.description: Syre closes the loop on textile waste. They use a chemical recycling process that restores old polyester garments into virgin-quality polyester fibers again and again. This built-for-scale method prevents waste and cuts emissions drastically. The result? A radically new supply chain for fashion that doesn’t cost the Earth.

companies.name: Tandem PV
companies.one_liner: Catches the light a solar panel misses.
companies.solution: More efficient panels mean more clean electricity from the same land and the same grid connections, without a new application to file. That could make solar even cheaper and help it grow faster in places where land and grid access are limited. For a town that has waited years on permits and a place in the queue, the power would come from ground already approved and already paid for, sooner than anybody dared to plan for.
companies.problem: Most of the cost of a solar farm is in land, steel and installation, not the panels themselves, so more power from the same space makes a big difference. Tandem PV coats glass with a material called perovskite and laminates it onto standard silicon cells, catching light the silicon would otherwise waste as heat. The result is a standard-size module, so the same footprint of racking, cabling and crew time would yield more watts.

companies.name: Techcoop
companies.one_liner: Turns Vietnam’s small shops and farmers into financial powerhouses
companies.solution: TechCoop is a Vietnamese agritech company providing a digital platform that integrates financing, supply chain management, and market access for agricultural companies and smallholder farmers.
companies.problem: Across Southeast Asia, millions of small retailers from market stalls to family-owned shops operate almost entirely in cash, with limited access to banking or digital tools. This leaves them excluded from credit, growth opportunities, and the broader digital economy. Financial inclusion remains a massive untapped lever for regional development.
companies.description: Techcoop equips Vietnam’s mom-and-pop shops with smart point-of-sale systems, QR payment tools, and embedded financial services. These shops suddenly gain access to credit scoring, loans, and inventory management. All through a device as simple as a smartphone. It’s grassroots digitization that lifts entire local economies, starting with farmers and the neighborhood corner store.

companies.name: Terabase
companies.one_liner: Makes setting up solar power plants a digital delight.

companies.name: Teton
companies.one_liner: Gives nurses AI-powers
companies.solution: Teton offers a real‑time, AI‑powered patient monitoring system that keeps patients safe, eases nurse workload, and boosts care quality. Their platform integrates into existing routines and data systems to help staff move from reactive to proactive care.
companies.problem: Nurses are stretched thin (monitoring multiple patients with limited time and tools) leading to missed warning signs, burnout, and preventable complications in care.
companies.description: Teton installs sensors and smart cameras in patient rooms to monitor activity continuously. Their AI analyzes patient behavior (sleep, movement, risk of falls) and sends alerts to staff instantly. It acts like an extra set of eyes that allow nurses to be aware of issues before they turn critical.

companies.name: The Exploration Company
companies.one_liner: Building space logistics that everyone can use.
companies.solution: Access to space is limited to a few players. Rocket systems tend to be closed, costly, and built for single use. This restricts innovation, collaborative missions, sustainable access, and scalable research in orbit and beyond.
companies.problem: The Exploration Company is building Nyx, a modular, reusable spacecraft designed for cargo delivery to low‑Earth orbit and lunar destinations. It features open‑source APIs and refuelling capability in orbit. This makes space access more affordable, sustainable, and accessible to a broader range of users.
companies.description: The Exploration Company is building space vehicles for a collaborative future, making space exploration affordable, modular and sustainable through its reusable and refillable space craft.

companies.name: The Great Bubble Barrier®
companies.one_liner: Cleans up river trash with water bubbles that acts like a high-tech vacuum.

companies.name: Three Wheels United
companies.one_liner: Financing to bring electric mobility to emerging markets.

companies.name: Tipa
companies.one_liner: Putting an end to plastic packaging with functional and cheap biodegradable materials.

companies.name: To zero
companies.one_liner: Recycles lithium-ion batteries to recover vital materials and cut e-waste impact.

companies.name: tozero
companies.one_liner: Turns dead batteries into Europe’s next critical mineral supply chain.
companies.solution: Committed to recycling lithium-ion batteries, recovering essential materials like lithium, nickel, cobalt, and graphite, reducing the environmental impact of lithium-ion batteries, a major contributor to e-waste.
companies.problem: Europe needs vast amounts of lithium, graphite, cobalt, and nickel to meet its growing demand for electric vehicles and renewable energy. Most of those materials are imported, often extracted through harmful mining. Meanwhile, used batteries are often discarded or shipped abroad.
companies.description: Tozero is building Europe’s first end-to-end lithium-ion battery recycling plant, using a proprietary process that extracts critical minerals safely and efficiently. Their low-emission, closed-loop system transforms battery waste into raw materials for new batteries right where they’re needed. It’s the backbone of a circular, sovereign energy future for Europe.

companies.name: Traceless
companies.one_liner: Turns conventional plastic into a fully sustainable alternative that leaves no trace.
companies.solution: Develops innovative, bio-based materials that serve as sustainable alternatives to plastics, fully compostable and leaving no harmful traces in the environment
companies.problem: Plastic pollution is choking ecosystems and accelerating the climate crisis. Even bioplastics often require industrial composting and still take months to degrade. Meanwhile, packaging waste continues to pile up, especially in single-use formats.
companies.description: Traceless has developed a revolutionary material made from agricultural residues that behaves like plastic but decomposes like a banana peel: quickly, fully, and naturally. It needs no special conditions, leaves no microplastics, and emits up to 87% less CO₂ than conventional plastic. It’s packaging that protects products and the planet.

companies.name: Trawa
companies.one_liner: Gives small factories an energy trader.
companies.solution: If smaller businesses can buy energy as smartly as the biggest players, they can save money and make better use of their own solar and storage, counting panels and batteries as part of how they buy power. That could make clean energy pay off for many more factories and firms. Buying well would stop being something only size can afford, whoever happens to handle the contracts that week, in a business of any size, in any town.
companies.problem: Large companies have energy traders watching the market for the right moment to buy. Smaller businesses rarely do, so the price they pay is often set by whatever the market happened to be doing the week their old contract ran out. Trawa supplies electricity to mid-sized companies and uses its own software to buy in instalments spread across the year rather than in one contract on one day, reading each customer's usage, solar panels and batteries.
companies.description: Trawa uses software and algorithms to automate clean energy procurement, ensuring companies get optimal pricing, real-time insights, and access to 100% renewable energy. Allowing them to save up to 30% on electricity costs and tap into easy-to-access green energy.

companies.name: Trukkr
companies.one_liner: Reinventing supply chains, putting tech in the driver’s seat to move businesses faster than ever.

companies.name: Turaco
companies.one_liner: Insurance for the price of a soda
companies.solution: If this kind of cover reaches the millions of people already paying for loans and solar kits, insurance stops being a product for the few, and no longer needs an agent to travel out and collect it. A spell in hospital, or a death in the family, wouldn't have to push a household back into poverty. A shopkeeper could meet the bill, bury a parent properly, and still open again the next morning.
companies.problem: For families earning day to day, a standalone insurance policy is out of reach, so a hospital bill often means borrowing or selling something they need. Turaco builds small health and life cover into things people already pay for, like a loan, a solar subscription or a mobile wallet, for a few extra coins a month. The premium comes off the same monthly payment, and Turaco handles the sign-up and the claim behind it.

companies.name: TURN2X
companies.one_liner: Natural gas, minus the fossil part.
companies.solution: Europe has a huge network of gas pipelines, storage caverns, import terminals and millions of burners. Clean synthetic gas could keep all of that in use as the continent moves away from fossil fuels, and let sunny regions ship their solar energy through pipes to where it's needed. A kiln in the north could run on light that fell in the south, over the same connection it has always used, and the pipes already in the ground would carry it there.
companies.problem: Many factories run on equipment built for natural gas, with decades of working life left in it, and replacing it is expensive. TURN2X makes a clean version of that gas: it uses renewable electricity to split water into hydrogen, then combines it with carbon dioxide left over from biogas production, making a methane that flows through existing pipelines.

companies.name: Turntide Technologies
companies.one_liner: Creating advanced electric motors to drive down energy consumption from machinery.

companies.name: TurtleTree
companies.one_liner: What If, We Could Create Real Milk Without Animals??

companies.name: Twelve
companies.one_liner: Eliminates emissions by turning CO2 into essential products, like green jet fuel or plastic.

companies.name: TytoCare
companies.one_liner: What if, we build a device that lets patients perform common medical checks at home?

companies.name: Unacademy
companies.one_liner: What if, we could give everyone the same shot at higher education?

companies.name: UNDO
companies.one_liner: Capturing and storing CO2 in rocks for hundreds of thousands of years.

companies.name: Unobravo
companies.one_liner: Matches people to therapists and handles the paperwork
companies.solution: If finding the right support becomes quick and affordable, more people could get help early, before problems grow. Public services could then focus on the most serious cases, making mental health care work better for everyone. For someone in Italy, Spain or France who has finally decided to ask for help, the wait would be a matter of days rather than a place on a ranked list, and the cost would be known before the first conversation.
companies.problem: Finding the right therapist can be hard: public services have long waiting lists, and people often rely on a friend's recommendation and hope for the best. Unobravo matches people with licensed psychologists through a short questionnaire, offering a free first session and a fixed price for the rest. The questionnaire returns a short list from its own network, so the first conversation is with someone chosen for that person.

companies.name: Unspun
companies.one_liner: Remakes how clothes are made with sustainable and circular 3D weaving technology.

companies.name: UPSIDE Foods
companies.one_liner: What if, we could grow all our meat in a lab?

companies.name: Vaayu
companies.one_liner: A climate scientist embedded in every checkout.
companies.solution: Automated AI software empowering retail brands and businesses to track and cut environmental impact in real-time.
companies.problem: Retailers and consumer brands are under pressure to reduce emissions but tracking environmental impact across sprawling supply chains, materials, and logistics is slow, manual, and riddled with data gaps. By the time companies act, it’s often too late.
companies.description: Vaayu is the first automated software platform that calculates, forecasts, and reduces emissions across every retail transaction in real time. Vaayu gives brands instant visibility and actionable insights to decarbonize operations at speed and scale. It’s like having a climate scientist embedded in every checkout.

companies.name: Valence Labs
companies.one_liner: Using AI to discover and develop new drugs.

companies.name: Vara
companies.one_liner: Using AI to improve breast cancer detection.

companies.name: Variant Bio
companies.one_liner: Studies rare genes to find medicines for everyone
companies.solution: Studying the full diversity of human genetics could uncover new medicines that benefit everyone, because a variant only becomes a medicine if someone sequenced the people who carry it. It could also set a fairer standard for research, where the communities who make discoveries possible share in their rewards. Sequencing a population would come with terms agreed in advance, and a share of whatever follows.
companies.problem: Most genetic research is based on people of European ancestry, held in a handful of wealthy-country biobanks, so many valuable insights from other populations are missed. Variant Bio partners with communities around the world whose members have unusual health traits, studies their DNA with consent, and shares the benefits of any discoveries back with those communities. Traits like resistance to a common disease point to rare protective variants that can become medicines.
companies.description: Variant Bio identifies genetic outliers, people and communities with rare traits like disease resistance or extreme longevity, and partners with them to discover new therapies. Through ethical, benefit-sharing collaborations, they build more inclusive genomic data and translate it into breakthrough drugs. It’s precision medicine that starts with global justice.

companies.name: Vaxess Technologies
companies.one_liner: Getting vaccines in the body through patches - not needles.

companies.name: Veir
companies.one_liner: Creates a new way to transmit electricity using advanced superconductors, making power delivery more efficient.

companies.name: VEIR
companies.one_liner: Supercooled cables that solve the energy bottleneck.
companies.solution: VEIR delivers 5-10x the electrical power over the same transmission corridor with superconducting systems aimed at enhancing energy infrastructure for data centers, renewable energy integration, and utility grids.
companies.problem: The clean energy transition is stalled not by supply, but by transmission. Wind and solar power are booming, but the outdated grid can’t carry the electricity to where it’s needed. Building new lines takes over a decade, massive land use and they’re still not efficient enough.
companies.description: VEIR builds superconducting power lines that can carry five to ten times more electricity than today’s cables. They work by cooling the wires with liquid nitrogen, which removes resistance and makes energy flow freely. These compact lines fit into existing corridors, so grids can upgrade without waiting years for new construction.

companies.name: Vema
companies.one_liner: Hydrogen made simple, clean, and abundant.
companies.solution: Vema uses deep earth chemistry to turn ordinary rock into a constant, low cost source of clean hydrogen. Their approach could deliver abundant hydrogen to fuel the global energy transition.
companies.problem: The clean energy transition needs hydrogen, but current methods are too expensive and limited. Green hydrogen made from renewable electricity is costly, while conventional methods release large amounts of carbon. The world needs a cheaper and cleaner way to unlock hydrogen at scale.
companies.description: Vema produces Engineered Mineral Hydrogen by stimulating natural reactions in rocks underground. This process creates hydrogen directly in place, without electrolysis or fossil fuels. It is scalable, carbon free, and projected to cost less than one dollar per kilogram.

companies.name: Verdagy
companies.one_liner: Turns water into green hydrogen with next-gen electrolysis technology.

companies.name: Verdox
companies.one_liner: Develops goodbye-to-carbon-emissions-tech for aluminum production

companies.name: Via Separations
companies.one_liner: What if, we could save energy by separating chemicals with membranes rather than heat?

companies.name: Vibrant Planet
companies.one_liner: Decides which acre burns on purpose.
companies.solution: Faster, better planning could help communities, landowners and agencies work together to protect forests before fires strike, and re-plan each season rather than each budget cycle. That could mean healthier landscapes, safer homes and fewer devastating fire seasons. For a county that has lived through one, it is the difference between watching the weather every summer and knowing the work on the hillside above town is already done.
companies.problem: Preventing wildfires means planning where to thin forests and carry out controlled burns, but that planning is slow, done by hand and often stops at property lines. Vibrant Planet uses satellite mapping and fire modelling to help land managers plan the most effective treatments across whole landscapes. What comes back is a sequence of thinning and burning projects, ranked by how much risk each one actually removes.

companies.name: VIDA
companies.one_liner: What if, we use satellites to plan out electricity grids in the world's poorest areas?

companies.name: Vind AI
companies.one_liner: Finds the wind farm hiding in a map.
companies.solution: Faster planning means more wind farms get built, and sites once dismissed as too difficult might get a second look. That could speed up the growth of wind power at a time when every year counts. A team could weigh many sites for the effort a single one takes today, and the years now spent finding out late that a place does not pay would be spent building instead, on ground nobody had bothered to look at twice.
companies.problem: Planning a wind farm means juggling turbine positions, costs, cables, grid connection and local impact, spread across different software and consultants. Each change can take weeks. Vind AI brings it all into one model, so developers can test new layouts and see the business case in a single step. Moving a turbine returns the yield, the cable routing and the revenue together, instead of another round of files sent out by email.
companies.description: Vind AI has created a software platform that uses AI to design wind farms. It combines layout, yield, cost, and environmental data in one place. Developers can test hundreds of scenarios in minutes, compare outcomes, and plan projects faster and more accurately.

companies.name: Vinted
companies.one_liner: What If, We Make Second Hand Clothing The First Hand Choice?

companies.name: Vira Health
companies.one_liner: What if, we use digital therapeutics to help women through menopause?

companies.name: Visibuilt
companies.one_liner: Fungal asphalt that cuts CO₂ and heat.
companies.solution: Visibuilt creates a natural binder for roads that works like bitumen (the glue that holds asphalt together in road building) but comes from fungi instead of fossil fuels. It lets roads be built cooler, cleaner, and with a fraction of the emissions.
companies.problem: Most of the world’s roads are held together by bitumen, a sticky binder made from oil. It has to be heated to extreme temperatures before use, wasting huge amounts of energy and releasing CO₂. Every new road locks in more emissions.
companies.description: Visibuilt has found another way. By using fungi and natural fermentation, they make a binder that can hold roads together at room temperature. It replaces fossil oil with a bio-based alternative, cutting both heat and carbon from road building.

companies.name: Voize
companies.one_liner: Writes patient records so nurses can focus on care
companies.solution: With a major shortage of care workers on the horizon, giving time back to staff matters hugely. If paperwork no longer eats into every shift, care workers can focus on what they do best: looking after people. For the person in the room, that is a few more minutes of somebody's attention on an ordinary afternoon, given by someone who is not already counting down to the paperwork waiting at the end of the round.
companies.problem: Care workers spend a big part of every shift writing up notes, at a shared desktop at the end of a round or after the shift ends, time taken away from the people they care for. Voize lets them simply speak into a phone after a visit, and its speech recognition turns what they say into the right entries in the resident's record. It runs on the handset, in care vocabulary and many accents, and syncs when a connection returns.

companies.name: Volta Greentech
companies.one_liner: What If, Cows Stopped Farting And We Could Save The Ozone Layer?

companies.name: VunaPay
companies.one_liner: Fair pay for farmers, right away.
companies.solution: VunaPay provides instant payments to farmers as they deliver their produce to Agricultural Cooperatives, bringing reliable income and financial stability to thousands of smallholders.
companies.problem: Hundreds of millions of smallholder farmers in Africa are stuck in poverty traps, underpaid for their crops and overlooked in climate finance. At the same time, climate change is accelerating land degradation, and traditional carbon markets rarely reach the grassroots where change starts.
companies.description: VunaPay digitizes produce logistics and financial management for cooperatives, enabling transparent and timely payouts to farmers. It brings reliable income and financial stability to thousands of smallholders.

companies.name: Wala Digital Health
companies.one_liner: What if, we build a digital marketplace for developing countries to manage, share and request blood?

companies.name: Waterplan
companies.one_liner: Helps companies take control of water waste and water use in their facilities and supply chains.

companies.name: Watershed
companies.one_liner: Giving companies a way to measure, report and reduce emissions in just a few weeks.

companies.name: Wave
companies.one_liner: Banking redesigned to include every African.
companies.solution: Building extremely affordable financial infrastructure for Africa.
companies.problem: In many parts of Africa, banks are out of reach and mobile payment systems come with high fees. Sending or receiving money often costs too much and takes too long, especially for small transactions and remittances.
companies.description: Wave is building a mobile-first bank for the underserved. It offers free deposits, free bill payments, and only 1 percent fee for money transfers. Its agent network and app ecosystem make sending and receiving money as easy as sending a text. It’s financial inclusion that works for everyone, not just the wealthy.

companies.one_liner: What if, we build a cutting-edge digital health platform for the largest country in Africa?

companies.one_liner: Boosts crops with carbon-cutting, yield-boosting solutions that turn farm productivity up to eleven.

companies.name: Wildtype
companies.one_liner: What If, We Could Make Sushi Without Killing Fish?

companies.name: Windfall Bio
companies.one_liner: Methane pollution turned into farm nutrients.
companies.solution: Naturally transforming climate-harming methane into an agricultural resource.
companies.problem: Methane is an urgent climate threat. It traps over 80 times more heat than CO₂ over 20 years. At the same time, synthetic nitrogen fertilizer is polluting, carbon-intensive, and expensive for farmers. This leaves both our atmosphere and soils under strain.
companies.description: Windfall Bio harnesses naturally occurring microbes that eat methane and exhale nitrogen. Their biotech platform deploys these microbes in methane-rich environments (like farms or waste sites) to eliminate pollution and produce organic, soil-ready nitrogen. It’s a dual impact: cutting climate-warming gas while regenerating farmland, all powered by nature’s own chemistry.

companies.one_liner: What if, we enlist AI to help restaurants reduce food waste?

companies.name: Woebot Health
companies.one_liner: AI-assisted mental health care, available on your phone.

companies.name: Worn Again Technologies
companies.one_liner: Putting textiles back into the supply chain by making clothes fully recyclable.

companies.name: Wota
companies.one_liner: Turns wastewater into a cost cutting resource with home-based, small-scale water recycling systems.

companies.name: XAG
companies.one_liner: Increases farm production and reduce waste through the use of flying drones.

companies.name: Ÿnsect

companies.name: Zero Acre Farms
companies.one_liner: What if, we make oil from sugar instead of from vegetables?

companies.name: ZeroAvia
companies.one_liner: Developing hydrogen-powered aircraft with virtually zero emissions.

companies.name: Zipline
companies.one_liner: Using drones to deliver vital medicines to rural and inaccessible areas.

companies.name: ZwitterCo
companies.one_liner: Membranes that can make even the foulest water clean and re-usable again.

faqs.question: Whoa, slow down. What is all this?
faqs.answer: The Norrsken100 is an annual selection of the most promising early-stage startups solving global challenges at scale by outperforming the legacy models that created them. They shape what comes next. In other words: It’s 100 ways to fix the future. Pretty cool, right?

faqs.question: Who made this list?
faqs.answer: The Norrsken/100 is curated by Norrsken Foundation. It is compiled from nominations made by our partners. This year, our team processed 1,400+ nominations from 80 hand-picked nomination partners, among them some of the world's most prominent venture capital firms, academic institutions and NGOs in the field.

faqs.question: What is Norrsken?
faqs.answer: Glad you asked! Norrsken is a global community of founders, funders, thinkers and advocates united by a shared belief in innovation and entrepreneurship as tools for positive change. Norrsken manages award-winning Norrsken House hubs in Amsterdam, Barcelona, Kigali, Brussels and Stockholm. Norrsken's five funds have raised more than 750m USD to back exceptional entrepreneurs who combine profit with positive global impact: Norrsken VC, Norrsken22, Norrsken Evolve, Norrsken Launcher and Norrsken Africa Seed Fund. Norrsken is a non-profit, non-partisan and non-religious foundation. It was founded by [name], co-founder of payment services unicorn Klarna.

faqs.question: What are the criteria for being on the list?
faqs.answer: The Norrsken/100 consists of: Early-stage impact companies, meaning companies where positive global impact is an intrinsic and non-negotiable part of the business model. High-potential ventures that aim to leverage scalable technology to do business and drive positive impact. Businesses with a scalable business model and a proven ability to combine growth with positive global impact. Companies that have delivered at least an MVP product to market and/or raised at least Seed and at most series B-funding.

faqs.question: What’s an Impact Startup?
faqs.answer: An impact startup is a fast-growing company where positive impact forms an intrinsic and non-negotiable part of the business model. We are particularly interested in companies that leverage scalable technology to solve global problems. We define impact as driving meaningful and measurable progress towards one or several of the 17 Sustainable Development Goals.

faqs.question: Why isn’t Company X on the list?
faqs.answer: It’s hard to say! It might be that our team looked at the company and decided it wasn’t right for the list, at this point in time at least. Or - it might not have been nominated at all. We’ve done our best to source as many relevant nominations as possible, to cover a wide spectrum of companies, problems and solutions. But there will of course be cases we’ve missed, and calls made where you’ll disagree with us. If you’re a startup founder - don’t hesitate to let us know if you think you deserve a spot on the list.

faqs.question: Is the list ranked? Are there winners?
faqs.answer: The Norrsken/100 is not ranked. Simply being on the list means you’re a winner. It means you’ve been selected by one of the world’s leading venture capital firms, academic institutions or NGOs as a future impact unicorn - a company that could positively impact the lives of 1 billion people.

faqs.question: This is a great project! How can I contribute?
faqs.answer: Glad you like it! We’re always looking for more partners - to help us source relevant nominations, to give the Norrsken/100 companies the attention they deserve, and to build cool things around the initiative throughout the year. Whatever shape that takes, get in touch and we’ll make something happen. Email us at info@norrskenfoundation.org.
